# UI control intentions for left-to-right writing

This inventory starts with the public controls and uses Andrews's Canvas to infer the writing purpose of each grammatical choice. The design reference is writing with pencil and paper. A writer normally puts the sentence on the page from first to last, just as a speaker normally says its parts in sequence. A prepared stem or saved clause can be retrieved earlier in the interface and still occupy a later position in the sentence. For each example, ask what is already on the page, what the writer needs to put down next, and whether the choice adds material at the right edge or revises an earlier position. Written order, interface action order, and grammar-engine execution are recorded separately. The coverage checklist records which claims have browser, renderer, Owner, or Canvas evidence and where that evidence stops.

The writer’s place on the line is the starting point for judging a control. If the writer has **Calaquih** on the page and wants to add the purpose clause in Andrews’s **Calaquih in tēmictizqueh.**, the next written piece is **in**, followed by **tēmictizqueh**. The workbench may ask the writer to prepare or retrieve that final clause first. The inventory records that step as preparation and asks whether the control still makes it clear what goes next on the line. If a choice changes something already written, record the earlier position it changes. If Andrews determines what appears there, look for a way to show the effect of the writer’s choice. [Purpose-clause example and browser sequence](#marking-a-purpose-clause)

Three questions guide the inventory. **Where am I on the line?** Start from the last piece the writer has put down. **What can I decide here?** Offer the choices Andrews gives the writer and show where each takes effect. **Do I need to go back?** An earlier position may need revision, as when the writer adds **Ahō-** before the existing **micqueh**. Show that move explicitly. Preparing a reusable clause in History is like having it on a separate slip of paper. Its place on the new line comes from the construction the writer chooses. [Negative and antecessive example](#negative-and-antecessive-browser-record) · [History controls](#revisiting-earlier-builds)

Treat the end of the written line as the writer’s place. A control for continuing should help the writer put the next piece there. A control that changes an earlier piece should show which piece it will change. A choice that only identifies the grammar should show what it identifies, even when the letters stay the same. This gives each control a purpose in the writing process, regardless of where the control sits on screen.

For each possible addition, first ask whether the writer needs to **do** something or **see** something. In **Calaquih in tēmictizqueh.**, placing **in** between the clauses is the consequence of the chosen construction. A preview can show that placement. In **Ōquittac Petoloh.**, the writer can choose which participant **Petoloh** refers to while the written words stay the same. The contact selector serves that decision. These are different needs at the writer’s place on the line. [Purpose](#marking-a-purpose-clause) · [Supplement contact](#choosing-what-a-supplement-refers-to)

## Deciding what belongs before Make Result

| What the writer needs before accepting the line | What the evidence suggests |
| --- | --- |
| See where the next piece goes | Extend the existing **Staged order** display for **Calaquih → in → tēmictizqueh**. The writer supplies the clause and marker. The display can show their positions before Make. [Purpose example](#marking-a-purpose-clause) |
| Know whether a selection still needs a click | Clarify **Next voice layer · automatic** when its only option is still unselected. In the **Nipachōlo** draft, selecting it staged the **tla** operation and enabled Make. [Verbal voice example](#choosing-verbal-voice) |
| Find the existing action for the next piece | Label the direct-address role in terms of the prepared command and the following addressee. The visible selector and History already made **Tlā xihuāllauh, Tlālīxcapān!** in that order. [History supply example](#revisiting-earlier-builds) |
| Carry a visible spelling choice into the accepted line | Check the handoff to Make for **Matrix supportive-vowel variant**. The spindle draft requested omission and accepted **Mailacatl.** The grammar can write **Malacatl.** when it receives the licensed choice. [Compound example](#choosing-the-relation-within-a-nominal-compound) |
| Use a finished expression in a distinct way | The author of **Huitztzilōpōchco** wants to use an accepted name to write a consecrated place. A separate action is worth considering if that use still needs its own entry after the existing place formation path can accept the exact name. [Name-to-place example](#forming-a-personal-name) |

**Make Result** accepts the prepared expression. The proposals above concern what the writer can choose, see, or retrieve while preparing it. Each proposal uses the position affected in the written line as its test. [Full proposal table](#possible-changes-to-the-writing-workflow)

## Find controls by what you want to do

The shared action column asks what several paths can do with the same control. The last column records which distinctions still matter when those paths arrive at the same step. The area entries retain the exact labels and visibility conditions.

| Writer action | Area and existing controls | Shared action | What still needs to carry through |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Start with a stem or recover prepared material | Source · [Enter or accept a Source](#entering-and-accepting-a-source) · [History](#revisiting-earlier-builds) | Bring material into the current draft. Use the existing retrieval action wherever the same saved item is eligible. | A typed stem, a saved whole, and a saved constituent have different provenance and may authorize different operations. |
| Add a prepared piece to the line | Grammar · [Combine Results](#joining-saved-clauses-in-grammar) | Reuse the saved-Result chooser across grammatical roles. Put the role prompt at the point where the piece belongs on the line. | Preserve which role the writer selected, the accepted identity of the piece, and its written position. |
| Decide who a piece refers to | Grammar · [Supplement contact](#choosing-what-a-supplement-refers-to) | Use a participant choice where the Owner authorizes multiple eligible references. | The Peter paths both reach **Ōquittac Petoloh.** The subject and object contacts remain distinct in Analysis and replay. [Topology comparison](andrews-grammar-os-topology-map.md#L84) |
| Revise something already written | Result · [Part and edit actions](#revising-a-constituent-of-an-accepted-result) | Choose the affected part once, then show the actions available for that part. | Preserve the exact occurrence and whether the action revises a draft or the accepted expression. |
| Check the order or reason for a form | Analysis · [Accepted analysis](#reading-the-accepted-analysis) | Group the views around the same accepted expression. | Preserve the separate jobs of written order, relationships, and formula explanations. |
| Retrieve a piece for the current role | History · [Revisiting earlier builds](#revisiting-earlier-builds) | Reuse the path for supplying an eligible saved piece. | Keep the difference between supplying a piece to an open role and reopening a build as Source. |
| Move to another stage or change the display | Navigation and settings · [Workbench controls](#moving-around-the-workbench) | Keep stage access and display preferences in a consistent location across writing routes. | Stage changes follow the active draft. Display choices serve how the writer inspects it. |

### Check whether two controls can share an action

| Area | Compare these existing paths | Disposition and what must survive |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source | Typed Source acceptance, saved whole, saved constituent | Keep typed admission and saved retrieval distinct. A saved capture can supply permissions and derivational ancestry that typing the same letters cannot reproduce. |
| Grammar | Saved-piece pickers across clause relations | Share the picker interface where possible. Keep role eligibility, contact, and position from the selected construction. |
| Result | Change, Add, Reorder, Remove on an accepted occurrence | Keep the single **Part** entry point. Keep the four edits distinct because each changes the line differently and has its own eligibility. |
| Analysis | Linear, Diagram, and Sentence views | Keep the shared accepted Result as input. Keep the views distinct because one expression can have identical letters and different relationships. |
| History | Use as Source, Add to pending sentence, continue an earlier build | Share selection of the saved build. Keep the actions distinct because they set the current Source, fill a pending role, or move to an earlier point in History. |
| Navigation | Source, Grammar, Result, and History | Keep the persistent stage controls. History retrieves material from any stage, while the three stage controls change the current working panel. |
| Settings | Simple and Analysis, accepted output scope, private study preferences | Keep display depth, paradigm scope, and study consent distinct. Display changes how the writer looks at the line. Output scope changes which related forms are displayed. Consent governs recording. |

## How a control serves left-to-right writing

| Writer's task | Example from the inventory | What the interface should help the writer see |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Enter the next written piece | **tem → temō** | Which character was inserted and where. This has direct browser evidence. |
| Pick a different written construction | **Chicōme-Cōātl** and **Mācuilxōchitl** illustrate two calendar structures | Where the boundary between numeral and day sign falls. The two examples establish distinct structures, with availability for any given pair determined separately. |
| Revise material to the left of an existing piece | **Micqueh. → Ahōmicqueh.** | Which prefix choices are staged and in what order the grammar will write them. |
| Revise an accepted line or revise its draft | [Calaquih in tēmictizqueh.](#revising-a-constituent-of-an-accepted-result) | **Clear marker** takes the captured **in** out of the draft while keeping both clause captures. The remaining purpose choices still need to authorize the line. Removing the entire attachment would keep only **Calaquih**. The accepted browser **Part** menu offered only the whole for this example. |
| Specify the relation between identical written pieces | **Ōquittac Petoloh.**, with Peter as subject or object | Which pronoun refers to Peter. The topology-map comparison shows both contacts in Result Analysis. |
| Choose what happened first | **Ōtlapāntihuetz.** | Which event happened first while the grammatical pieces retain their written order. |
| Choose an optional spelling at a join | **tēuc → ciztli** can give **tēucciztli** or **tēcciztli** | Show the alternatives the writer can select for the end of **tēuc**. [Canvas §2.13.4](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L1969) |
| See a required spelling at a join | **on → pēhua** gives **ompēhua** | Show that the **n** becomes **m** before **p**. The checked Owner route gives ordinary writing as its only option, so a readout can explain the result. [Canvas §2.11.7](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L1883) · [Writing controls and verification](#entering-and-accepting-a-source) |
| Look up a form while keeping your place | **Output scope** on the accepted line | This works like consulting a reference beside the page. The paradigm rows are for reading. To write a form from the table, return to the draft and make the corresponding Grammar choices. [Accepted Result view](#reading-the-accepted-analysis) |
| Inspect an obligatory realization | **mīmicqueh** | That the grammar supplies the affinity copy in this plural. Andrews's optional onlooker variants illustrate when a choice belongs to the writer instead. |

These distinctions suggest different interface treatments. A selectable control serves a licensed choice. A readout can show a grammar-determined position or form. The existing Analysis views are the first place to check for an interpretation that leaves the written words unchanged. Where the writer needs that information before accepting a result, inspect the current staged feedback before proposing an addition.

Preparation order and assembly order can differ in the same journey. **Huel** was prepared first and attached later to the left of the command. In the purpose example, the piece prepared first is written last.

**A writing-order check before Make.** In the purpose example, the current steps are to prepare **Tēmictizqueh.**, prepare and continue **Calaquih.**, retrieve the purpose clause, then supply **in**. The writer's pencil-and-paper question at the last step is where **in** goes. An inferred improvement is to reuse the **Staged order** readout for the accepted inputs in their pending positions, **Calaquih → in → tēmictizqueh**. The readout would show the consequence of the current **Clause order** and marker choices. It would give the writer a way to check the line before committing it without adding a placement choice. The retained browser record establishes the capture and marker steps. The current Source structure renderer builds this strip for ordinary or cooperating adjectival modification, eligible shared-reference supplementation, and modifier-first intensification. Its draft projection has no Purpose branch. That makes Purpose a candidate for extending the existing readout. The retained pre-Make Grammar snapshot shows the two captured clauses, the marker, and the selected order as separate facts. It shows no combined line in that Grammar view. [Canvas and browser sequence](#marking-a-purpose-clause) · [Draft projection and supported patterns](../../src/ui/composition/structure_design.mjs#L102) · [Staged order renderer](../../src/ui/composition/structure_design.mjs#L220)

These browser examples show three different jobs for the controls. Some enter the next piece directly. Some let the writer place prepared material or revise an earlier position. Some let the writer specify a grammatical relationship that the letters alone cannot show. The proposal for a pre-Make prefix readout concerns the second job. A pre-Make contact readout would serve the third only where existing staged feedback leaves the choice unclear.

### A possible new action at the right edge

**Use this name in a place name** is a candidate action beside **Reranking**. The writer starts with **Huitztzilōpōchtli** already written and decides to use that god’s name for a consecrated place. The checked path prepares the god name, looks for a locative use in **Reranking**, and checks **Operation** for **Form a place or associated-person name**. Reranking requires a typed locative-matrix Source. The navigator withheld the exact current-Result binding, while the public Operation menu still offered a formation-choices entry. In the browser, that entry exposed the place-name kind and left **Formation** invisible. The direct Owner fixture succeeded with the exact name, **co**, and adverbial usage. [Canvas consecrated place name](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L24692) · [Reranking dependency](../../src/ui/rendering/nominal_construction_presentation.mjs#L3548) · [Exact place-name fixture](../../src/tests/reader_56_2_hummingbird_left_name.test.mjs#L40) · [Current navigator probe](#forming-a-personal-name)

The proposed action would carry the exact selected name into a draft for the adverbial place-name use and focus **Formation**. In this example the checked Owner request needs both that use and **co**. The nominal Grammar request already maps **Place / gentilic result → place name** to adverbial usage, so the handoff can reuse that mapping. The exact saved-name binding fails during preliminary validation. The separate public formation-choices entry reaches the kind field and leaves the ending choice invisible. A handoff would need to stage the validated place-name use with **co** and show **Huitztzilōpōch → co** before Make. [Existing usage mapping](../../src/ui/rendering/nominal_construction_presentation.mjs#L8615) Andrews supplies the omission of the standalone ending. The writer reviews the draft and accepts it with **Make Result**. This proposal is an inference from the Canvas example and the workbench. It depends on a validated binding for that exact name. Once the binding is available, check the ordinary Operation route first. A dedicated control would be useful if the writer still needs a way to carry the name forward directly from **Reranking**. [Operation staging](../../src/ui/composition/build_task_menu.mjs#L213)

**What the action would ask the writer to decide.** Andrews gives different locative matrices for different prepared names. **Huitztzilōpōch → co**, **Mācuilxōchi → c**, and **Xipe → tlān** show why a general action labeled **Add -co** would misstate the task. The writer decides to reuse the name for a place. The staged **Formation** field can offer the Owner-licensed continuations for that exact name. The tested Huitztzilōpōchtli binding authorizes **co** with adverbial usage and rejects **c**. The other endings here are Canvas examples, with their public routes unverified. Atom `ACI-P622-L024-17D8F2BAE7` assigns the embedding rule to the god-name place-name Owner. The example Atoms `ACI-P622-L029-60EA61F4F2`, `ACI-P622-L028-DCF3186552`, and `ACI-P622-L033-85F22F2C34` record the three written joins in the order cited here. The distinct proposed action is the direct handoff of the exact prepared name from **Reranking** into that draft. If continuing the name through **Operation** gives the writer the same next step without losing the name, the existing controls cover this writing need. [Canvas §56.5 locative contrasts](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L24691) · [Atom ledger](../ANDREWS_ATOM_LEDGER.json) · [God-name place-name Owner](../../src/core/classical/nuclear-owner-specs/classical-personal-name-nnc-god-name-place-name-embed.mjs) · [Exact -co and rejected -c](../../src/tests/reader_56_2_hummingbird_left_name.test.mjs#L40) · [Existing stage-only route](../../src/ui/rendering/owner_journey_presentation.mjs#L6300)

The proposed handoff has a concrete writing check. With the accepted **Huitztzilōpōchtli** displayed, activate the handoff and check that the draft identifies the same captured name and shows the planned join **Huitztzilōpōch → co**. The accepted line should still read **Huitztzilōpōchtli** until the writer presses **Make Result**. Then the next accepted line should read **Huitztzilōpōchco**. Apply the same check through the ordinary **Operation** entry if it becomes available. If that path already carries the exact name and shows the join before Make, a separate action would duplicate the writer’s next step. This is a proposed interface check. The passing Owner fixture also refused a copied name, the underlying compound supplied directly, and **-c** for this exact name. These cases define what the handoff should preserve when it presents the draft. The navigator probe and the same-session browser run supply route evidence. The browser could select the existing formation-choices alias and the place-name kind, but its **Formation** field was hidden and Make left the accepted name displayed. This gives the proposed handoff a concrete interface problem to solve. [Owner fixture](../../src/tests/reader_56_2_hummingbird_left_name.test.mjs#L40) · [Saved-name navigator evidence](#forming-a-personal-name)

## Operation menu captions for starting a construction

These captions appear in **Grammar → Operation** when the corresponding native construction route is available for the current Source or eligible saved Result. Choosing one opens the construction's choices. The linked entries give the writing example and conditions for the subsequent fields. [Construction caption map](../../src/ui/composition/build_task_menu.mjs#L8)

| Displayed operation | What the writer opens |
| --- | --- |
| Make a noun from a verb | [Nominalization](#building-a-nominal-clause-from-a-verbal-predicate), such as building **cuīcatl** from singing material. |
| Form an adverbial clause | [Adverbial use and context](#giving-an-adverbial-expression-its-context), including where a modifier belongs. |
| Embed a noun in a verb | [Nominal embedding](#incorporating-a-noun-into-a-verbstem), such as putting **xōchi** before the seeking stem in **Nixōchitēmoa**. |
| Express honorific, reverential or pejorative attitude | [Verbal attitude choices](#expressing-respect-in-a-verbal-clause). |
| Form a nominal compound | [Nominal compound choices](#choosing-the-relation-within-a-nominal-compound), including the connection between the first and second stems. |
| Form an affective noun | [Nominal attitude choices](#expressing-regard-or-disparagement-in-a-nominal-clause) for the new noun. |
| Change quality | [Adjectival quality choices](#choosing-the-relation-within-a-nominal-compound), including whether the modifier expresses intensity or distribution. |
| Form a cardinal-number construction | [Number and count choices](#writing-a-numeral-or-a-counted-unit). |
| Form a calendar date | [Numeral, sign, and boundary choices](#writing-a-calendar-date). |
| Form a personal name | [Personal-name choices](#forming-a-personal-name). |
| Form a place or associated-person name | [Place and associated-person choices](#writing-a-place-name-or-a-name-for-its-inhabitants). |
| Make a verb from a noun | [Denominal choices](#building-a-verb-from-a-noun) for the material after the nounstem. |

The navigator also supplies the captions below. Their availability follows the current input and its pathway state.

| Navigator caption | What the writer opens |
| --- | --- |
| Make a noun clause / Make a pronoun clause / NNC quantitative predicate | [Nominal Source and analysis](#identifying-the-nounstems-form), including a noun, pronoun, or quantity used as a predicate. |
| Change sentence type or polarity | [Sentence choices](#sentence-composition-from-a-saved-verbal-clause) for an existing nominal expression, including revision of the left edge for negation. |
| Add a modifier / Make an adverb | [Adverbial choices](#giving-an-adverbial-expression-its-context) for attaching a modifier or preparing an adverbial expression. |
| Add a particle / Make a particle / Choose a negative expression | [Particle choices](#selecting-particles-and-particle-sequences) for preparing material or supplying it in a sentence. |
| Change voice | Open [Next voice layer and Following voice layer](#choosing-verbal-voice) for an eligible exact verbal Result. The binding starts from its existing voice chain. |
| Add a description | [Adjectival modification](#placing-an-adjective-or-a-describing-clause), where the writer specifies what a description applies to and where it goes. |
| Build a relational noun | [Relational noun choices](#writing-a-relational-noun), such as choosing the possessor written before **pan**. |
| Form a place or inhabitant name | Navigator caption for the [place and inhabitant route](#writing-a-place-name-or-a-name-for-its-inhabitants). The native construction caption is **Form a place or associated-person name**. |
| Clause comparison | [Comparison routes](#placing-a-resemblance-with-iuhqui) for relating prepared pieces by similarity, degree, or another licensed comparison. |

[Navigator caption formatter](../../src/ui/composition/build_navigation_model.mjs#L193) · [Option rendering and pathway state](../../src/ui/rendering/owner_journey_presentation.mjs#L11633)

**Operation groups.** The navigator groups routes under **Clauses and sentences**, **Formation and conversion**, **Modification and combination**, and **Particles**. The groups guide the writer to different tasks: prepare a clause, change a stem, join prepared pieces, or build or attach a particle. An otherwise available route with no mapped group can appear under **Other operations**. These are menu headings. The writer chooses an operation inside the group. The model separately defines **Form or transform stems**, **Build or change a clause or particle**, and **Relate or combine units** as purpose references. The consolidated menu uses the group mapping for its displayed headings. [Menu groups and purpose references](../../src/ui/composition/build_navigation_model.mjs#L122) · [Menu route projection](../../src/ui/composition/build_task_menu.mjs#L50)

**Which piece the operation will use.** Where both a saved expression and editable Source material are present, a caption can end in **current Result**, **current Source**, **Source editor**, or **formation choices**. The renderer adds these qualifiers when overlap or the current input calls for it. They give the writer a chance to check which draft will supply the material before selecting the task. For the ocean-shore example, the distinction matters because the writer wants to carry forward the complete prepared **huēi ātl** before adding the shore matrix. The exact-Result continuation preserves that analysis as an input. The caption logic is verified in code. The complete ocean-shore journey remains unverified in the public menu. [Menu qualifiers](../../src/ui/composition/build_task_menu.mjs#L144) · [Fixed-expression writing example](#incorporating-a-noun-into-a-verbstem)

**When the menu combines routes or keeps both.** The native neutral construction is the direct **Make a noun clause** or **Make a verb clause** route. If the same direct action is already offered by the navigator, the menu treats the neutral option as its alias. The generic nominal-construction caption can also disappear when multiple concrete formation tasks are available and the generic route has neither a validated binding nor evidence that it accepts the current Source. Other overlapping entries keep their distinct addresses. For example, a writer carrying **huēi ātl** into the shore formation needs the route that preserves the prepared expression. A **Source editor: [text]** label identifies a route that would instead take the editor material. This is menu source evidence. The exact shore journey remains open in the browser. [Direct route and generic-caption filter](../../src/ui/composition/build_task_menu.mjs#L121) · [Exact fixed-expression example](#incorporating-a-noun-into-a-verbstem)

**Picking the same operation after revisiting a line.** The menu looks up the live route again when selected. If the active Source has withdrawn it, the old menu entry cannot stage it. After continuing a saved clause, the old operation label may still be selected while its binding has been cleared. Selecting the same clause operation then refreshes that binding and rebuilds the partner picker. In **Calaquih in tēmictizqueh.**, returning to **Calaquih.** means that the writer still needs to supply the purpose clause for this draft. The retained browser record shows the capture and order for that construction. The current menu suite passed all 18 tests, including stale-address rejection and restaging a clause operation. The exact repeated selection on **Calaquih.** remains unverified. [Live route and binding checks](../../src/ui/composition/build_task_menu.mjs#L173) · [Focused menu tests](../../src/tests/build_task_menu.test.mjs#L67) · [Purpose writing sequence](#marking-a-purpose-clause)

**Operation and Grammar for a retained Writing Source.** The organizer has a conditional Writing Source mode. In that mode, **Operation** offers only available operations for the validated exact transcription Source, and Grammar exposes only choice IDs from its current binding. The focused menu fixture creates an exact particle-group transcription Source, exposes the transcription operation alone, then withdraws it when the binding is copied or the native option is disabled. Andrews’s **zan → oc → cencah** shows the writing problem this path can serve: keep the order of adjacent particles while choosing how to write them. The fixture verifies operation filtering for its **za** and **oc** Source. It supplies no public entry or transcription proof for the exact Canvas phrase. Public entry into this mode remains unverified. [Canvas particle sequence](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L22845) · [Writing Source mode and Grammar filtering](../../src/ui/composition/choice_design.mjs#L49) · [Focused menu case](../../src/tests/build_task_menu.test.mjs#L316)

**When a task can appear.** The consolidated menu normally includes enabled options from the current Source and construction selectors. For an exact Result, it can also reopen the native **Change quality**, **Form a calendar date**, or **Form a place or associated-person name** entry when the matching Owner binding is validated. The calendar binding lets the writer start with either half of a date and still write **Ēi → Calli**. A route omitted from the menu can have an explanation in **Requirements**. The reader should check availability on the particular saved piece: the existence of an operation caption does not establish that it can accept every Source. [Menu availability checks](../../src/ui/composition/build_task_menu.mjs#L53) · [Calendar role example](#writing-a-calendar-date)

**Availability labels behind Operation and Requirements.** The navigator uses **Ready now** for an available route with no known details to supply and **Choose details** when the writer can enter a route that needs choices or another captured piece. Both groups are interactive in the underlying selector. **Needs a Result** identifies a route that requires a compatible saved Result. **Needs another Source** identifies other unresolved input prerequisites. **Not compatible** indicates that the Owner classified the current input as incompatible. Those groups supply guidance and disabled native options. The operation menu itself filters available options, and **Requirements** can explain why the task is missing. The labels guide the writer to the next action. They do not decide written order. [Navigator groups](../../src/ui/rendering/owner_journey_presentation.mjs#L8625) · [Availability classification](../../src/ui/rendering/owner_journey_presentation.mjs#L8687) · [Group and option rendering](../../src/ui/rendering/owner_journey_presentation.mjs#L11633)

**Focused Operation menu check.** All 18 tests in `build_task_menu.test.mjs` passed. The cases check how the menu distinguishes two routes that share a grammatical operation, rechecks availability on selection, and offers adjectival, calendar, and place-name choices when a test Result has the validated binding. The passing place-name case establishes what the menu does when the binding is available. The exact **Huitztzilōpōchtli** probe still found no such binding for that name. [Menu fixture](../../src/tests/build_task_menu.test.mjs#L154) · [Exact god-name comparison](#forming-a-personal-name)

**How to read the evidence.** A browser receipt establishes only the controls and states it records. A settled snapshot can confirm what was selected without fixing the order of clicks. Proposals about what would make writing easier remain design inferences. The representative journeys show how to compare the page with the interface. Conditional controls can also be documented from their renderer when a journey has not exercised them.

**Changing Grammar while keeping the typed Source.** In the ordinary and pronominal noun branches, the native event handler accepts the visible, writable noun controls for the subject, state, possessor, stem relation, predicate form, and plural connector, as well as the shared sentence controls. It reads those values with the current exact nominal Source and stages the operation again. The fields under Source identity are excluded from that handler. For a prepared house stem, selecting a first-person possessor in Grammar asks for **no-** at the left of **cal**. The writer is changing how the retained stem is used. The noun Source itself is still **cal**. On the denominal branch, changing the operation path clears the former object-person selection before restaging. This matters when the verb to be written licenses a different object from the previous path. These checks establish the event path and staging boundary. Each Owner still determines which choices are available for the exact Source. **Which choices the typed operation plan generates.** Grammar creates inline fields for required choices and selected choices still supported by the current binding. It also offers available alternatives for ordinary and pronominal nouns and retains recovery alternatives while an ordinary noun draft needs work. Some optional choices get an inline field as soon as the Owner supplies them, including the verbal **Finite connector** and the admonitive plural ending. Fields already assigned to native Grammar controls stay there. Inline selectors offer only available options and restore a still-available selection. For **icn-īuh**, the observed required **Possessor** supplies **no** at the left of **cnīuh**. The optional finite connector instead concerns the number position after the verb stem and tense. These examples show why the order of fields in the operation plan should be read separately from the order of the resulting letters. The renderer establishes the inclusion rule. The attested-cell browser record establishes the required possessor interaction, and the verbal sections describe the evidence for the two optional endings. **When a verb choice changes another field.** On the typed verb Source path, the handler associates the edited field with its grammatical choice even if Grammar has moved it out of its original panel. Selecting **Mood** or changing the subject recomputes the available tense, singular connector, and admonitive ending before staging. Andrews’s **Mā titlacuahtin.** illustrates why the writer may need to review both ends of the line. The admonitive puts **Mā** before the clause, while an eligible plural ending goes at the right edge. The writer chooses the mood and any still-licensed ending. The handler also clears a previously chosen singular connector after changes such as Voice or derivation, which can make the former ending inapplicable. These are code findings about the pending choices. In the typed route, the handler carries the projected admonitive ending into the draft if the edited mood and subject still support it. Otherwise it removes that ending before staging. In the continuation route, the native field needs a current exact Owner binding with more than one available ending. When that condition fails, the renderer hides and disables the field and clears its value. On paper, this is the point to revisit the right edge of **Mā titlacuahtin.** if the writer changes the mood or subject after choosing the ending. The exact browser sequence for changing these dependent fields together is open. For **temō**, the writer enters **t → e → m → ō**. This identifies material for a later operation. | Retain in this pass |
| Long vowels | Source, next to stem entry | Open the character helper. Canvas §2.2 explains vowel quantity and the transcription passage specifies the macron spelling. A compact disclosure provides access while leaving space for the stem. | Retain in this pass |
| ā, ē, ī, ō | Inside Long vowels, with an active stem field | Enter the chosen long-vowel character. In **temō**, **ō** occupies the final stem position. Choosing the macron is a spelling action based on the stem's vowel quantity. | Retain in this pass |
| Use this Source | Source entry, when available | Submit the prepared starting material for Source admission and expose its applicable build routes. This is the interface's point for accepting the input. | Retain in this pass |
| Clear | Source entry, when available | Clear the input and return the workbench to its waiting state. This is an interface edit affecting the draft as a whole. | Retain in this pass |
| Edit Source / Choose or edit Source | Source disclosure in layouts that group the entry fields. The workspace organizer uses **Edit Source**. | Reveal the draft controls to enter material or revisit a stem. Opening the disclosure is an interface action. A change physically takes effect wherever the edited stem belongs in the expression. | Retain in this pass |
| Writing | Hidden spelling group in the Source shell. The renderer can move it into Grammar for a validated transcription operation. Ordinary Source entry has no standalone Writing editor. | Request one of the authorized written variants for the supplied material. | Retain in this pass |
| Elide vowel | Same conditional group when the exact transcription binding includes an elision | Request the licensed elided form. Starting with **zā oc**, the writer keeps **zā** and omits the opening **o** of **oc** in solid **zāc**. | Retain in this pass |

**Source group names used by assistive technology.** The shell groups **VNC verbal** and **NNC nominal** under **Classical Nahuatl basal unit**. The editor section is named **Classical source: stem or particle**. **VNC built-in verbstems** contains **Try an example**. **Identified source properties** contains the starting verb’s **Source VNC Valence** and can expose **Source voice** and **Source nonactive formation** for an eligible causative. **Long vowels for the active stem field** identifies the character helper’s group, and **Writing choices** identifies the conditional spelling group. These names locate the controls. The active stem and its intended operation determine which fields the writer can use. For **quīxohua**, the starting voice and formation belong with the prepared Source. The later Grammar voice concerns the expression the writer will make from it. **The entry field and its readouts.** The three editable inputs are **Stem**, **Embed**, and **Matrix**, with their availability set by the Source mode. A rendered internal segment can also have a textbox role, but the generated segment is read-only. In the retained **ihcihui** snapshot, the writer could edit the actual **Stem · typed** textbox. A separately rendered readout of a recognized segment would be for inspection. This distinction matters when using **Long vowels** to revise the written material. **Writing or correcting a vowel in place.** The helper labels each key **Insert ā**, **Insert ē**, **Insert ī**, or **Insert ō**. For a single stem it targets **Stem**. In **Embed + matrix** the active field determines which piece receives the letter, with the embed as the default. A key inserts at the caret or replaces the selected text, returns focus to that field, and marks Source as pending. A read-only or disabled target disables the keys. In the observed **tem → temō** journey, the vowel goes at the right edge. The same insertion rule can correct an earlier letter while keeping the material to its right. In isolated Chrome, the writer entered **cuauh** in **Embed** and **hua** in **Matrix**, moved the Matrix caret left three times, opened **Long vowels**, and clicked **Insert ē**. The helper wrote **ēhua**, kept **cuauh** in Embed, and returned focus to Matrix. An initial attempt using Home produced **huaē**. The successful arrow-key run verifies insertion at an earlier position in the active compound field. A second isolated run selected the first **e** in **ehua** with the arrow keys, then clicked **Insert ē**. The helper replaced that letter, producing **ēhua** with the remaining **hua** and the separate **cuauh** intact. The writer chooses whether to show the omission, and the grammar supplies the licensed spelling. Atom `ACI-P052-L020-B62AAD1010` assigns the general rule to the vowel-elision Owner. The renderer requires an authorized transcription binding and a projected elision choice before exposing the checkbox. The Owner fixture exercises **oc → c** and rejects the same transformation outside the licensed group. Public reachability of this writing-source route remains unverified. **Writing at a consonant join.** For an exact compound Writing Source, the **Writing** menu starts with **Ordinary writing**. When the Owner detects the licensed boundary, it can also offer **Use c before c / qu**, **Use h before c / qu**, or **Use h after delabialization**, according to the sounds on either side. Andrews gives **tēuc + ciztli → tēcciztli** and also attests **tēucciztli**. The writer has both pieces and revises the last consonant of the first at the join. The Owner assigns the choice to that exact segment. For **Use h before c / qu**, Andrews illustrates **Mēxic + co → Mēxihco**. For **Use h after delabialization**, he gives **iuccāuhtli**, **iccāuhtli**, and **ihcāuhtli** as variants. In both cases the edit is at the last consonant of the left piece. Atom `ACI-P052-L010-C54302F544` assigns the exposed **/kʷ/ → [k]** option to the consonant-phone-shift Owner. Atoms `ACI-P050-L022-A33747C200` and `ACI-P050-L025-12876984C1` assign both routes to **h** to the regressive-dissimilation Owner. The first applies to two neighboring **k** sounds. The second applies once the left consonant has become **k**. **Why the consonant options depend on a prepared compound.** The Owner attaches each option to the last sound of a specific left constituent. For **tēuc → ciztli**, that is the final labialized consonant of **tēuc**. The **c** option changes that sound. The **h** option for the same kind of boundary first applies that change and then the dissimilation. The focused compound test passed again and checked the ordered dependency. It also passed the same sound sequence as raw, unsegmented input and received only **Ordinary writing**. The writer therefore needs an analyzed join before the menu can offer the optional boundary spelling. The proposed readout can identify which prepared boundary will change. The fixture establishes the condition for an analogous compound, while public entry and selection for **tēuc** and **ciztli** remain unverified. **Actual labels for the consonant alternatives.** The writing renderer contains an uncalled Lesson 2 helper with the captions **Use cc** and **Use hc**. The mounted **Writing** selector instead reads the validated transcription binding’s option labels. For **tēuc → ciztli**, look for **Use c before c / qu** where the Owner licenses the **cc** spelling. The **h** option after delabialization has its own Owner caption. The helper captions supply no additional public controls. **One spelling choice at a time.** In a validated transcription draft, **Writing** and **Elide vowel** share one Owner selection. Checking elision stages its licensed option. Editing **Writing** clears the checkbox and stages the menu’s choice. When the selected choice is elision, the menu shows **Ordinary writing** alongside the checked box. For **zā oc → zāc**, the checkbox therefore carries the change at the join. A readout of the effective spelling beside these existing controls could make that relationship clear before **Make Result**. The renderer verifies how the two controls share the selection. The proposal follows Andrews’s elision example, and the exact public draft still needs observation. **A join the grammar supplies.** Andrews gives **on + pēhua → ompēhua**. The writer has **on** before **pēhua**. At that boundary the grammar supplies **m** immediately before **p**. Atom `ACI-P050-L014-BF59E2C201` gives the condition, and `ACI-P050-L015-7913C1CB36` records the example. The condition belongs to the regressive-assimilation Owner. [Atom ledger](../ANDREWS_ATOM_LEDGER.json) · [Regressive-assimilation Owner](../../src/core/classical/transcription-owner-specs/classical-regressive-assimilation.mjs) The compound Writing Source stores the original morphemes and can carry a required boundary rule into the **Ordinary writing** result. It builds optional menu entries separately. With a required boundary the useful information is what changes at the join. The current renderer has no separate **n / m** selector for that rule. The focused runtime check reached and passed the assertions that **Ordinary writing** was the only choice, that the issued spelling contained **mp**, and that the formula retained the original sounds. The same test failed later when the Source validator accepted a substituted copy of the assimilation frame. The menu and spelling assertions therefore have runtime evidence, while the broader identity check remains failed. **Source button states.** Browser captures show **Enter a Source before applying it** and **No Source to clear** as the accessible labels on the two disabled buttons in an empty workspace. The renderer also sets **Use pending Source** when the draft has unapplied changes, and gives a class-selection instruction when admission still requires a class. These labels belong to the same two buttons. **Which Source is in use while editing.** **Not applied** marks the pending input. If a different Source is already in use, the message can name it while telling the writer to use the edited Source or choose its class. **Applied** names the committed stem. **Result source** identifies a retained whole, and the associated guidance can tell the writer to continue with an accepted Source and route. For **temō**, this makes the point of review explicit after typing or changing the final **ō**. The guide is a status readout. **Use this Source** is the action that applies the edit. All three focused first-use guidance tests passed. The exact restored-route message is documented from source. **When a Source class is required.** With Andrews’s **temō** entered, the retained browser run showed **Verbstem class · fixed**. That class describes how the stem will inflect later. The admission helper asks for **Verbstem class** when the current verbal class selection has no accepted value. For ordinary nominal input it asks for **Nounstem class** only when Source admission returns the explicit missing-class reason. The attested Source families such as **Teticpac** can instead take their own route. If a class is required, **Use this Source** waits for it, and choosing the class prepares the input for Apply. The current focused suite passed the ordinary noun’s missing and supplied class cases and the fixed/pronominal cases. Eleven other cases stopped in the simulated presentation environment. Three lacked `getClassicalFirstUseNextAction`, and eight lacked `document.querySelectorAll`. Those cases supply no verification for the verbal, restored, and edit transitions they were meant to cover. **Writing a stem from slash-delimited sounds.** The existing **Stem** field and the two **Embed + matrix** inputs also accept the app’s compact sound notation. At **Use this Source**, the handler checks every active field before replacing any sound entry with written letters. A rejected field stays pending and is marked invalid. **Check Source notation**, **Check Embed notation**, or **Check Matrix notation** tells the writer where to correct it. The accompanying hint distinguishes an unrecognized token, an unclosed token, and mixed spelling and sound notation. In the **/k** case the hint says **Close each sound token with /.** The error refers to the rejected input value, so changing that input clears the old marking. [Source error messages and reset](../../src/ui/shell/classical_shell.mjs#L5367) For the **cal** material in Andrews’s **ā-cal**, the runtime accepts **/k/a/l/** and supplies **c → a → l**. This gives the writer a way to enter sounds in order before the grammar uses the written stem. The direct Owner check also rejects an unclosed token such as **/k**. Andrews’s transcription conventions ground the sound-to-letter distinction. The app’s compact input syntax is its own convention. The focused panel fixture stopped on a missing presentation helper, and the public apply sequence remains unverified. **Readouts beside the editable stem.** The Source reconstruction note and **Typed internal morphemes** explain what the app recognized. The renderer gives each internal segment a read-only textbox role and shows the group for a verbal nuclear clause with constitution parts. For a Source such as Andrews’s **iht-o-ā**, the writer enters the stem in **Stem**. The internal segments explain its analysis in order. Keyboard users can submit Source with **Enter** where the entry handler accepts it. This is the same submission as **Use this Source**. The field roles and keyboard shortcut come from code. **When the Source editor opens on its own.** The editor opens for waiting, pending, or invalid input. It also opens when **Add**, **Ask about this**, **Leave clause implicit**, or **Address someone** needs material. Clicking the Source stage opens it directly. This lets the writer reach the fields at the moment the draft requires another piece. In the Peter example, the new piece will go after the verb despite being prepared first in the retained journey. After a successful Source application, the organizer can fold the editor and return focus to the disclosure. The auto-open conditions come from code. **Starting a different piece.** **Clear source and return Build and Result to waiting** is enabled when either the draft or the committed Source exists. Its click handler clears Source evaluation. The retained §17.4 walkthrough used it after making **Petoloh.**, then entered **itt-a** and made **Quittac** as a separate piece. The later attempt to open **Make a sentence** stopped at the operation menu. On paper, **Petoloh** will follow **Ōquittac** in the final sentence, even though this workflow prepares the name first. ## Identifying the Source before writing a clause

| Control | Where and when | Action and inferred purpose | Sweep disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| VNC · verbal nuclear clause | Source type chooser | Start with a verbal predicate. In **Nitlacua.**, Andrews's verbal formula accounts for the object pattern, stem, and tense, alongside the subject. | Retain in this pass |
| NNC · nominal nuclear clause | Source type chooser | Start with a nominal predicate. In **nocal**, Andrews's nominal formula accounts for possessive State and the stem, alongside the subject. | Retain in this pass |
| Try an example | Source, when the example picker is exposed | Supply an example to start the draft. The picker offers a quicker way to begin with known material. The verbal picker uses the canonical stem inventory and enters the stem in the whole-stem field. Its handler refreshes the suggested class and valence for the new stem. The nominal **Canonical nounstem** picker can also stage a specialized Source analysis when the entry supplies one, such as attested-place for **Teticpac**. The writer reviews the staged Source before applying it. [Verbal picker](../../src/ui/composer/composer.mjs#L9833) · [Nominal staging and Source use](../../src/ui/composer/composer.mjs#L12162) · [Canvas Teticpac](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L19968) | Retain in this pass |
| Verbstem class | Verbal Source, with availability depending on recognition | Identify the stem's class when the application needs that choice. Canvas distinguishes classes by the relation between their imperfective and perfective forms. In the isolated Analysis-mode check, recognition of **temō** marked the control **Verbstem class · fixed** and disabled it. | Retain in this pass |
| Meaning of this source | Conditional verbal Source field for unresolved lexical identity | Choose the intended sense of **pachihui**. Andrews §25 contrasts becoming full or satiated with becoming pressed down or sunken. The letters entered in the stem field can stay the same while the choice establishes which derivations are appropriate. | Retain in this pass |
| Initial i analysis | Conditional verbal Source guide | Identify **Real i**, **Supportive i**, or **Context-sensitive i** where the app requests the analysis. In Andrews's **tla-(iht-o-ā)** example, **i** drops in **tlahtoa** and survives the reflexive boundary in **mihtoa**. This affects the join at the left of the stem. | Retain in this pass |

**Initial i at the stem edge.** The writer identifies how the opening vowel behaves in context. The finite Owner adapter carries this choice as `source-initial-i` and restores it as a distinct Source selection. The topology map records public Make and fresh replay for real-i **Ninihtoa** and supportive-i **Ninohtoa**. Each retained Linear and Diagram, and the Owner round trip retained the chosen Source analysis. This is retained public proof for those two values on that route. The separate contextual value and frequentative continuation still need their own public evidence. **Identifying the stem before choosing a command opening.** Andrews analyzes ‘to hurry’ as **(ihc-i-hui)** in §25.2 and gives **Xihcihui.** and **Mā xihcihui.** in §9.7. The runtime request for bare **ihcihui** asked for **Initial i analysis** before it would build any of the command variants. The paired command checks then used the segmented Source and supportive **i**. In **Mā xihcihui.**, the opening **mā** comes from the introduction choice. The analysis of **i** concerns the later join with the subject marker inside **xihcihui**. The Source guide and the introduction selector serve separate decisions at those two written positions. The exact browser flow across both choices remains unverified. [Canvas stem analysis](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L8141) · [Canvas command pair](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L3680) · [Supportive stem fixture](../../src/tests/reader_25_2_initial_i.test.mjs#L4) · [Runtime command contrast](#selecting-particles-and-particle-sequences)

**When Initial i is a readout or a choice.** The guide checks the actual stem and valence. It shows a fact for a Source beginning with **i** or **ī**. With no canonical classification it opens **Initial i analysis** at **Choose an analysis** and requires a choice. If the canonical analysis licenses several realizations, the select instead starts at its derived default and filters the options to the licensed values. With a single established analysis the select stays hidden and the fact can explain the stem. This is the guide's rendering logic. For the command on **ihc-i-hui**, it explains why the starting stem analysis can be settled before the writer chooses whether to put **mā** left of **xihcihui**. [Source guide visibility and defaults](../../src/ui/composer/composer.mjs#L9319) · [Canvas command](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L3680)

**Returning to Initial i from a blocked draft.** The missing-analysis reason for unclassified **ihcihui** maps to the Source guide’s **Initial i analysis** select. If that field is available, Result recovery labels the action **Go to Initial i**. The action points the writer back to the stem analysis and leaves the command’s introductory particle to the separate Grammar field. The runtime probe established the missing-analysis reason, and the renderer establishes the destination and caption. The actual recovery click for this command remains unverified. [Block-to-field mapping](../../src/ui/rendering/surface_authority.mjs#L1709) · [Recovery caption](../../src/ui/rendering/surface_authority.mjs#L1789) · [Source field](../../src/ui/shell/classical_shell.mjs#L632)

**What the writer sees before recovery is needed.** In a fresh Chrome session, I chose **Analysis**, typed **ihcihui** in **Stem**, and pressed Tab. Source showed both **Verbstem class** and **Initial i analysis**. **Use this Source** was disabled and asked for the class first. The initial-i guidance was already visible beside the typed stem. This run establishes that the ordinary fresh-entry journey can stop in Source before any Result recovery action is offered. In a follow-up isolated run, selecting **B** enabled **Use this Source** while **Initial i analysis** still showed **Choose an analysis**. Clicking **Use this Source** then gave **Applied Using (ihcihui).** Thus the observed class prerequisite controls admission here, while the initial-vowel prompt concerns later generation. A further isolated run opened **Grammar** after admission. **Operation** contained only **What would you like to do?**, and **Make Result** was disabled with **Choices pending**. The snapshots showed no **Go to Initial i** button. In that run the writer could apply the stem but could not start the verbal build with the outstanding analysis. In a paired fresh browser run, choosing **Supportive i** before applying Class B **ihcihui** exposed **Make a verb clause**. Selecting it showed **Ready** and enabled **Make Result**. The two runs locate the public difference at the initial-i choice before Source admission. The selected analysis was a test input, and the run stopped before Make. In the two human-object examples, the written **tē-** goes before either causative stem. The meaning choice affects what follows: **pach-i-hui-tiā** for satiation and **pach-o-ā** for pressure. The exact field offers **pressed down, sunken, or settled** and **full, satiated, or satisfied**. It appears when the Source requests a lexical selection and the option IDs match its inventory. A changed stem or invalid selection clears the old value. Three focused tests passed for both readings and the missing-meaning case. They verify that the chosen Source meaning carries into the causal-formation inventory. The fixtures check **pach-i-huī-tiā** for satiation and **pach-o-ā** for pressure, each excluding the other. The satiation target has **ī** in the runtime fixture, while the cited Canvas example transcribes **hui**. The fixture corroborates the distinction in formation. The spelling difference remains open. Andrews describes pre-**tiā** length as usual in §25.2, which does not settle this specific printed form. A targeted search of the local workspace did not locate the original page image. Resolving the vowel length requires PDF page 212, printed page 197. The searchable text of an online copy also reads **hui** on that page. The page image was unavailable through the browser tool, so that text comparison does not settle the typography. Any subsequent causative choice has to follow the newly selected reading. The handler establishes the transition. The Source UI fixture describes cases for a hidden, stale-bound, or forged choice. ## Compound Source entry

| Control | Where and when | Action and inferred purpose | Sweep disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stem (mode button) | Source stem structure, selected initially in the shell | Use a single field to supply a whole stem. The button selects an entry layout. The separate Stem field holds the text. | Retain in this pass |
| Embed + matrix | Source stem structure | Switch to separate fields so the writer can identify the two pieces of a compound Source. | Retain in this pass |
| Embed | Source in Embed + matrix mode | Enter the first piece. In **cuauh + ēhua**, enter **cuauh** here. | Retain in this pass |
| Matrix | Source in Embed + matrix mode | Enter the second piece. In **cuauh + ēhua**, enter **ēhua** here. | Retain in this pass |

**Composition and interface order.** Andrews §28.2 puts the matrix after the embed in a governed compound. The retained §2.5 public check used **Embed + matrix**, supplied **cuauh** and **ēhua** with their noun classes, and staged the nominal compound operation before Make. The written result was **Cuauhēhuatl.** The order of the two fields corresponds to the written order. Class selection and Make establish the construction and its ending. They have no separate position as clicks on paper.

**Returning to one input.** Clicking the Source mode button **Stem** disables and clears both **Embed** and **Matrix**, marks Source for reevaluation, and focuses the whole-stem field. The personal-name renderer uses the same mode setter without clearing values when the raw **Source structure** changes to a one-clause family. In that case the two inputs become inactive and can keep their text. For **cuauh → ēhua → tl**, switching entry mode does not combine **cuauh** and **ēhua** into a whole stem. The writer supplies the whole form explicitly if that is what the new draft needs. An isolated Chrome run entered **cuauh** and **ēhua** in the two fields, clicked **Stem**, and observed a blank whole-stem field with focus. Both inactive inputs were empty. Reopening **Embed + matrix** gave two empty fields and focused **Embed**. This verifies the manual mode switch. The automatic personal-name switch is code evidence. [Browser receipt](/tmp/ui-intent-source-switch.json) [Source mode button handler](../../src/ui/composer/composer.mjs#L12209) · [Mode setter](../../src/ui/composer/composer.mjs#L9888) · [Personal-name mode switch](../../src/ui/rendering/nominal_construction_presentation.mjs#L3720)

**Explain the effect of switching entry modes.** With **cuauh** and **ēhua** typed, the writer has supplied the two materials for **Cuauhēhuatl.** Clicking **Stem** prepares a blank field and clears those entries, as the browser retest shows. The shell labels the button **Stem** and its group **Source stem structure**. The button markup supplies no explanation of that clearing action. Conditional wording beside the existing mode choices, such as **Switching to Stem clears these two entries**, would help a writer who wants to revise the join understand what the click does. This is a design inference about draft editing. Andrews’s spelling at the join still belongs to the compound formation. In **Āltepētl.**, the same entry layout supplies **ā** then **tepē**, and the two are equal conjuncts under Andrews §31.7. The retained calibration browser record shows **Embed** and **Governing matrix** for the first line and **Equal conjuncts** for the second, both after Make and after reopening. The Source labels identify entry positions before the writer has chosen how the two stems relate. ## Choosing the relation within a nominal compound

**Supplying the right side after preparing the embed.** For an authorized **compound-nnc:embed-result** binding, Grammar creates **Matrix Source**. It starts at **Saved Result**. Selecting **Known nounstem** opens **Matrix nounstem** and **Matrix class**. These fields reset when the captured embed changes. Andrews’s **yamāncācuicatl** illustrates the written order **yamāncā → cuica → tl**. With the adjectival material prepared, the writer supplies **cuica** next. Its class is information about the matrix and governs the compound’s ending. Atom `ACI-P427-L028-479690C7EF` records the exact formula. The renderer establishes the field conditions. The current focused Owner test returned a null donor during setup, before it could exercise the matrix binding or verify the expected form. The public control sequence remains unverified. [Canvas §41.4](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L16599) · [Atom ledger](../ANDREWS_ATOM_LEDGER.json) · [Matrix fields](../../src/ui/rendering/owner_journey_presentation.mjs#L5581) · [Focused binding fixture](../../src/tests/reader_41_4_primitive_matrix_binding.test.mjs)

**Supplying the left side after preparing the matrix.** On an eligible matrix Result, Grammar can create **Embed Source**, starting with **Choose a Source**. Its options come from the binding. They can include a licensed stem, the already typed Source, or **Compound form**. That last choice opens a field labeled **Form** and named **Compound form** for assistive technology. An exact captured embed suppresses the picker. Andrews’s **xīlō → tzon** ‘maize silk’ illustrates the writing need: **xīlō** goes first on the page even when the writer has already prepared **tzon** as the matrix. Atom `ACI-P427-L009-A6782BF2F9` records the compound inside **xīlōtzontic**. The passing runtime fixture authorized **xīlō** as a compound-use stem for exact **tzon**, left its noun class unspecified, and rejected a copied matrix. The exact public picker and typing sequence remain unverified. **When Embed Source opens a text field.** The generated **Embed Source** selector starts with **Choose a Source** and offers the stem from an authorized declaration or **Compound form**, when supplied by the exact binding. Selecting **Compound form** opens the text field labelled **Form**, with the accessible name **Compound form**. A change of exact matrix Result clears the old text. Once an exact embed is captured, the primitive selector is hidden. The control lets the writer supply the left-hand piece even if the right-hand matrix was prepared first. For example, in the jar-and-ear compound, the jar material goes before **nacaz**. The renderer establishes these conditional fields. The example illustrates the written position, and the exact generated text-field sequence remains unverified. **A third field called Embed meaning.** For the spindle, mark **Compound-only Source → both constituents** to describe **ma** on the left and **il-aca** on the right. The renderer then renames **Compound-only meaning** to **Embed meaning** and opens **Matrix meaning**. Both offer **known** or **uncertain**. With only one constituent marked, **Compound-only meaning** applies to that constituent, whether it is first or second. With both marked, **Embed meaning** applies to **ma** and **Matrix meaning** to **il-aca**. These describe what is known about each hypothetical stem’s independent meaning. The integrated compound can still have the known meaning ‘spindle’. Atom `ACI-P298-L032-362BCFFA57` assigns the reconstruction and written compound to the unique compound lexeme Owner. **Browser check of the spindle join.** In isolated Chrome, enter **ma** and **il-aca** under **Embed + matrix**, choose the matrix class **tl 2-B (final a)**, and apply Source. Open **Form a nominal compound → Nounstem formation**, choose the embed class `tl-1-a`, set **Compound-only Source → both constituents**, and leave both certainty values at **uncertain**. The two **Embed meaning** controls were visible together. The certainty field showed **uncertain**, while the relation field showed **association**. Then select **Matrix initial i → supportive vowel** and **Matrix supportive-vowel variant → initial i absent in this compound**. The pre-Make snapshot showed both selections. Make accepted **Mailacatl.**, with the **i** still written at the join. Andrews’s **ma → l → aca → tl** and the focused Owner fixture demonstrate the intended absence. The browser read establishes a discrepancy on this route. In the code, the general nominal request reads both vowel controls and the compound-only analyses. At Make, the exact typed Source route rebuilds its selection record from that request. That record omits the matrix vowel analysis, the variant, and the compound-only analyses. The typed compound Owner request also omits those fields. The evaluator then defaults the variant to **retain**, which accounts for the written **i** in the observed Result. The paired **Tepoztli.** spellings below therefore confirm the displayed line for each setting. A follow-up checked the accepted addresses and the analysis they rebuild, as described below. ### Adjective quality and compound choices

| Control | Where and when | Action and inferred purpose | Sweep disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Quality | Grammar for adjectival NNC formation | Choose **Intensify** or **Distribute** where licensed for the existing adjective. **tepitōn → tētepitōn** adds **tē-** before the stem to express greater intensity. **huitztic → huihhuitztic** adds **huih-** before the stem to describe the referents individually. | Retain in this pass |
| Embed form | Conditional adjectival Source group in nominal compound Grammar | Use the adjective's general-use shape or its root where licensed. In Andrews's **iztācāpahtic**, the general-use shape supplies **-cā-** before the matrix **pah**. | Retain in this pass |
| Source reading | Conditional adjectival Source group in compound or affective Grammar | Identify a regular formation or an attested adjective. In **iztācāpahtic**, the written first piece uses the attested **iztā-** adjective. The request records this separately from selecting the root or general-use shape. | Retain in this pass |
| Embed intensity | Conditional nominal compound Grammar with an eligible adjective | Request an intensified first piece. Compare **celpahtic → cēcelpahtic**, where **cē-** appears at the left of **cel**. | Retain in this pass |
| Matrix intensity | Conditional nominal compound Grammar when an expanded matrix is offered | Request an expanded second piece. In **cecepalalahtic**, **cece** comes first, then **palalah**, the expanded matrix from **pah**. | Retain in this pass |

**Quality in written order.** The writer starts with a formed adjective and chooses the intended meaning. The grammar determines the copy at the left edge. Andrews §41.1 distinguishes the long-vowel copy from the glottal-stop copy and ties the latter to referents differentiated by location or shape. Atoms `ACI-P421-L005-302B46C947` and `ACI-P421-L018-1B6FFC6CC8-07` assign the respective rules to separate Owners. The renderer reads the Quality selection, and the evaluator maps it to the copy shape. The focused suite cited below includes both examples, but its quality case stopped before those assertions in the current run. Public choice availability remains unverified. **When the two intensity controls appear.** With an exact adjective Result and matrix prepared, the renderer tests the current compound request once with **Intensified** at the embed and once with **Expanded** at the matrix. It offers each control only when its own test is authorized. With **cel → pah** prepared, **Embed intensity** can add **cē** before **cel**. With the cold adjective and **pah** prepared, **Matrix intensity** can expand **pah** after **cece**. The saved-adjective address adapter records those two values separately. A writer can therefore prepare either constituent first, then choose which side needs a change when the Owner offers it. This availability comes from code. The focused test verifies exact restoration and does not exercise field visibility in Chrome. **Writing the final plural.** Start with **mo-ch** and **eh-huā**. Andrews gives **mochehhuātl** and **mochehhuāntin**. The plural has an internal stem change as well as a different ending. The writer's ending selection happens after Source entry and State and Number selection. The current Owner fixture passed for **mochehhuāntin** and **mochehhuātl**. In the plural it checks the matrix’s internal **n** separately from the requested **-tin**. The renderer enables **Plural ending** only for an absolutive compound with plural Subject. In the common-number comparison **mochehhuātl**, the writer does not need that control. The written contrast is **mo-ch → eh-huā → tl** versus **mo-ch → eh-huā → n → t-in**. Andrews's **īichcameh** and **cihuātēteoh** illustrate the other two endings on different compounds. Those examples do not establish that all three endings can be exchanged on a single Source. **Class, relation, and a known meaning.** The renderer collects the first stem's class and the relation separately. ## Sentence composition from a saved verbal clause

| Control | Where and when | Action and inferred purpose | Sweep disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Operation | Grammar. The consolidated menu displays **Apply a Source to see available operations** when empty and **What would you like to do?** when routes are offered. | Choose the kind of construction to prepare. **Make a sentence** brings sentence choices into view for an already built clause. Canvas distinguishes an expanded VNC and an assertion sentence (§§8.1, 8.3). | Retain in this pass |
| Constructions / Build from a stem | Conditional Grammar disclosure. The organized workbench calls it **Constructions**. | Open construction choices that use the stem in Source. The renderer hides it when the selector is disabled or has no eligible nonstandard option. | Retain in this pass |
| Construction / Operation for this Source | The same field in the stem-construction disclosure or Source-path layout | Choose a construction that acts on the entered stem. Calendar date and noun-to-verb formation are examples of such construction choices. The available-operation picker can also start with an exact already built Result, which is why the selected input matters. | Retain in this pass |
| Operation options with **current Result**, **current Source**, **Source editor**, or **formation choices** | In the consolidated Grammar menu when the renderer needs to identify the input or distinguish overlapping routes | Check which piece the operation will use before selecting it. **Source editor** may identify the actual typed stem. **Current Result** acts on the accepted piece, including its grammatical structure. | Retain in this pass |
| Find / Find [choice] / Find an example | In eligible searchable choice menus. The renderer keeps short non-navigation menus plain and excludes the verbal example selector. | Open a search field that filters offered forms or meanings. It keeps the selected option visible while the writer looks for another choice. Closing Find clears the search. | Retain in this pass |
| Requirements / Why unavailable | Grammar operation picker when the navigator reports unavailable operations. The shell label is **Why unavailable**. The organized workbench displays **Requirements**. | Inspect prerequisites or restrictions for unavailable operations. The disclosure gives the writer a chance to see which additional piece or grammatical condition a route requires before attempting it. | Retain in this pass |
| Effects | Grammar, for a selected navigator operation with declared effects and no active native stem construction | Open the description of what the operation produces, adds, or removes. This helps the writer understand the kind of change before Make. | Retain in this pass |
| Analysis (applied Grammar) | Grammar, when the applied account is Owner-issued | Open **Form** and **Structure** for the applied operation. This explains the accepted outcome while the writer reviews Grammar choices. | Retain in this pass |
| Antecessive ō# | Grammar, in the sentence choices where applicable | The checkbox requests the order prefix. **Which prepared material an Operation will use.** When two menu entries share an operation but point to different underlying fields, the renderer qualifies their labels with **current Source** or **formation choices**. After capturing an exact Result, the Result route can read **current Result**, and a separate editor route can read **Source editor: [text]**. Some native constructions also accept the exact Result and receive **current Result** themselves. The menu fixture checks an editor entry labelled **Source editor: ce-liā** alongside a Result-based route. It also checks that an authenticated place-name option is labelled **current Result**. **Make captions for prepared constructions.** The same Make button reads **Complete Build choices** and is disabled while these renderer branches are waiting for the applicable inputs. Its accessible name identifies the pending task.

| Accessible name | Pending draft |
| --- | --- |
| Make Result: Source construction | A deverbal noun, personal name, adverbial nucleus, or place/name construction prepared from Source |
| Make Result: Attitude formation | An attitude derivation awaiting an authorized preview |
| Make Result: Noun construction | A noun draft from verbal root stock, without a captured prior Result |
| Make Result: Nominal construction / Make Result: Negative assertion | An affective noun draft. The negative assertion caption applies when the flawed-subject construction is being used in its contextual sentence route. |
| Make Result: Make a verb from a noun | A denominal draft awaiting its requested operation path and subject, with a preview check where a prepared Source exists |
| Sentence choices applied | An already applied nominal sentence task whose exact input and choices still match. The visible disabled caption is **Applied**. |

These captions report what the button will apply, or what has already been applied. In the compound example, a writer can prepare **Cōnnacaztli.** and then select the formation that writes **ti → c** at the right edge of **Cōnnacaztic**. The Make caption describes that operation. The separate Grammar choice supplies the transformation. The condition table comes from code, while the compound journey records the accepted forms and the writer’s sequence. ## Identifying the nounstem's form

**Whole quantity predicate.** In **Source analysis**, choose this value for a prepared quantity predicate such as **miec** in Andrews’s **Cencah miec in quitquiqueh in teōcuitlatl.** The writer carries **miec** as one piece. In the finished line it follows **Cencah** and precedes the **in** that begins the following material. With the quantitative analysis active, the Source renderer hides the ordinary noun class guidance and shows **Class and internal form unclaimed. Session only.** The note describes how much the app has analyzed and whether it can restore this Source. Two focused runtime checks passed for staging and executing the exact **miec** Source. The separate quantitative-material test also passed. It accepted **Miec.**, kept the noun class empty and the decomposition unclaimed, and admitted that exact Result for later supplementation. This lets the writer continue from the quantity while leaving its internal structure open. Atom `ACI-P431-L031-DC6EAF4867` records the whole sentence as an example of ambiguity between modification and supplementation. A fresh isolated Chrome run used **Analysis → NNC nominal → Stem** (type **miec**) **→ Source analysis → Whole quantity predicate**. Source displayed **Class and internal form unclaimed. Session only.** The run then used **Use this Source → Grammar → NNC quantitative predicate → Make Result**. The accepted line was **Miec.**, with **Session only** beside it. In a second isolated run, the accepted **Miec.** had one **Session only** notice and no Result address. Reload returned to an empty workbench and displayed **This Result can’t be restored after reload. Apply a Source to start a new build.** The full Andrews sentence remains unverified.
