## Describing a Source with multiple objects

| Control | Where and when | Action and inferred purpose | Sweep disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| More objects | Native verbal Grammar object controls, for a VNC Source with a supported transitive valence | Reveal the controls for describing a stem with more than one object requirement. | Retain in this pass |
| Add object | Inside More objects, enabled below three active rows | Add a second or third object description. In Andrews’s **n-ēch → tē → tla** example, the descriptions supply ‘me’, ‘someone’, and ‘something’ before the stem. A new row identifies an input slot. The Owner decides where its morph belongs in the sequence. [Canvas and ordering rules](#describing-a-source-with-multiple-objects) | Retain in this pass |
| Object 2 / Object 3 | In each added row | Use **Specific** for a referent such as the **me** expressed by **nēch**. **Someone** and **Something** describe the nonspecific referents expressed by **tē** and **tla** in the example below. **Reflexive** takes its person from the subject. Andrews also describes **m-o → ne** for two reflexive requirements. The prepared stem and derivation determine which reflexive form the grammar writes. The example establishes possible written order, while the row reader establishes what the UI submits. [Canvas §23.5](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L7624) · [Row reader](../../src/ui/composer/source_objects.mjs#L14) | Retain in this pass |
| Person and number | In an added row when **Specific** is selected | Identify the referent’s person and number. **specific nonanimate (one or more)** sends a third-person common-number object. In the passing cluster fixture the stone keeps that meaning while its formal agreement is third singular. The separate finite **maca** fixture stopped at admission of its second caller object. The application rejects extra caller rows on a specific-projective Source when the request uses direct derivation. Causative and applicative requests pass this particular gate and still have their own checks. The ability to open **More objects** therefore establishes that the writer can describe a participant. It takes a licensed construction to realize that description as part of the line. [Application admission](../../src/core/classical/vnc_application.mjs#L9618) This verifies the underlying cluster distinction and leaves the full public path open. [Row reader](../../src/ui/composer/source_objects.mjs#L14) · [Focused cluster and finite fixtures](../../src/tests/reader_42_9_common_object_cluster.test.mjs#L10) | Retain in this pass |
| Remove last object | Inside **More objects**, enabled when an extra row is active | Take the last numbered description out of the draft. The handler reduces the active row count and hides the inactive row. The reader excludes it from the next request. The field keeps its value if the writer adds that row again in the same draft. In a cluster such as **nēch → tē → tla**, this is a revision to a participant description. The removed row’s number alone does not identify which written morph will disappear. [Row reader and removal handler](../../src/ui/composer/source_objects.mjs#L12) · [Draft row controls](../../src/ui/composer/source_objects.mjs#L77) | Retain in this pass |

**Where the extra rows are mounted.** Although the rows describe Source participants, the shell puts **More objects** beside the native Grammar **Object** selector. The row synchronizer controls the disclosure’s own hidden state from the current VNC type and native valence. A closed or hidden containing Grammar section can still make it inaccessible. The first browser check stopped before choosing an operation. The follow-up below verified that **Make a verb clause** exposes the disclosure. [Shell placement](../../src/ui/shell/classical_shell.mjs#L4298) · [Local visibility and row synchronization](../../src/ui/composer/source_objects.mjs#L30)

**Isolated browser observation after applying Source.** In fresh local Chrome, enter **cua**, set **Source VNC Valence → specific-projective**, click **Use pending Source**, and open **Grammar**. Before choosing the operation, the disclosure's grid was hidden. Selecting **Operation → Make a verb clause** exposed **More objects**. Open it, click **Add object** twice, and set **Object 2 → Something** and **Object 3 → Someone**. Both numbered rows were visible. The browser check stopped before Make. The separate Andrews example and Owner checks below establish the comparison with the written sequence. [Browser receipt](/tmp/ui-intent-more-object-applied.json)

**When a row stays available.** The disclosure is offered for verbal Sources with specific projective, nonspecific human, nonspecific nonhuman, or mainline reflexive valence. The row controls allow one to three descriptions. Switching temporarily to an inapplicable valence hides the extra-object controls and retains their rows. Editing the stem text resets the active count to one. The request reader passes numbered descriptions to the Owner. In the added rows, **Specific** opens **Person and number**, while a reflexive row takes its person from the subject already supplied. **Composition and interface order.** Andrews §23.5 orders object morphs by form. One example is **n-ēch → tē → tla** (‘me, someone, something’). Andrews explains that the sequence can leave derivational roles ambiguous and that some object requirements can be realized silently. The row controls let the writer specify the required objects. The application owns the written order and realization. Adding a row therefore describes the intended Source without choosing the corresponding morph’s left-to-right position. Andrews’s full triple-object example puts the cluster between the subject and the already prepared derived stem: **ti → nēch → tē → tla → caquītīltia**. The object description for **nēch** is first-person singular. Its position does not make it the mainline object. In this sentence **tē** has that role. Atom `ACI-P223-L006-4952CEF74C-02` records the formula and `ACI-P223-L006-4952CEF74C-04` records the role of **tē**. This is a Canvas witness for placement. The exact public make path remains unverified. [Canvas §25.12.3](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L8450) · [Atom ledger](../ANDREWS_ATOM_LEDGER.json)

**Which Source fields the writer uses.** The shell also declares **Intransitive**, **Transitive**, and **Bitransitive** tabs with slot-specific **Embed**, **Matrix stem**, and **Derivation options** controls inside the composer marked as an engine mirror. The mirror labels its chip groups **Object 1/reflexive** in slots A and B and **Object 1/object 2/reflexive** in slot C. The active Classical Source stylesheet hides that entire composer. The Source valence is available in the typed verbal draft. **More objects** is declared for the native verbal Source controls, with public reachability dependent on where the workbench mounts it. Those controls describe the Source, and Andrews’s rules place the corresponding morphs in the written form. [Engine mirror markup](../../src/ui/shell/classical_shell.mjs#L2481) · [Classical Source visibility rule](../../style.css#L12859) · [Public object fields](../../src/ui/shell/classical_shell.mjs#L4307)

**Why the row number and written position can differ.** The row number records which object is being described. Andrews orders the corresponding written morphs by grammatical type. The Atom ledger assigns four rules to the object-priority Owner. A specific projective object precedes a reflexive object (`ACI-P195-L005-A95D95FBD7`) and a nonspecific object (`ACI-P195-L006-B9D194F2A1`). A reflexive precedes a nonspecific object (`ACI-P195-L007-BD125D9B1D`), and nonspecific human **tē** precedes nonhuman **tla** (`ACI-P195-L008-52B5ADECCE`). Thus a writer who needs **n-ēch → tē → tla** describes the three participants, and the grammar determines the sequence before the stem. When the directional **huāl** is also requested, a separate passing case puts it between **n-ēch** and **tē**. A preview should therefore use the assembled prefix positions and show silent objects in Analysis without inserting a written character for them. In the focused run, 17 of 19 cases passed. The two productive continuation cases stopped at the exact-issued-Result check before testing the completed surface. This verifies the cluster ordering and the tested directional placement at runtime. The public check verifies staging the extra rows. Acceptance with those rows and the two continuation surfaces still lack passing evidence. ## Incorporating a noun into a verbstem

**After supplying a saved piece.** The picker’s **Add [role] Result** caption identifies the material missing from the selected binding. For a completed nominal incorporation binding, the renderer can retain the picker with a single accepted **NNC embed Result** or **Verb** entry and disable **Use this Result**. A separate readout lists the roles and projected words of the exact supplied inputs. When the exact completion still matches, the picker keeps its **Add [role] Result** label while showing the captured word in a disabled selection. Read the supplied-input display to see what is already in the draft. The accepted option identifies the **Verb** on the noun-first path or the **NNC embed Result** on the verb-first path. [Completed-picker labels and disablement](../../src/ui/rendering/result_persistence_presentation.mjs#L1767) With the verb prepared first for **Nixōchitēmoa**, the noun input supplies **xōchi**, which will be written before the matrix **tēmoa** despite being supplied later in that workflow. The readout helps the writer see what has been supplied. The disabled picker, accepted captions, and readout come from code. The public sequence for this exact pair remains unverified. [Canvas and Owner example](#incorporating-a-noun-into-a-verbstem) · [Supplied input readout](../../src/ui/rendering/result_persistence_presentation.mjs#L1680) · [Completed picker](../../src/ui/rendering/result_persistence_presentation.mjs#L1733)

**Capture order in the picker status.** After a successful capture, the status lists **Additional Result** before **Retained Result**. These labels identify which piece was supplied and which was already retained. In a verb-first draft for **Nixōchitēmoa**, the added **xōchi** material goes before the retained **tēmoa**. In a noun-first draft, the added verb still appears first in the status even though the writer puts it after **xōchi**. A role-labeled readout in written order could clarify both paths using the existing captured-input display. This is an inference from Andrews’s example and the renderer. The exact public status for both orientations remains unverified. [Canvas §30.2](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L10354) · [Accepted picker status](../../src/ui/rendering/result_persistence_presentation.mjs#L1783)

The multiple-object case received a null finite Result before it could inspect the matrix’s object slots. These failures leave the public handoff and replacement sequence open. An in-memory silver-first rerun loaded the split renderer modules and the relocated directional prefix helper. With a temporary renderer context supplied, it reached the current binding and visibility handlers. The fixture then stopped because it lacks the dependency that restores typed compound class options. This simulated run did not reach Result capture. The visibility handler is shared across nominal construction routes, so this setup failure gives no evidence that a silver-first writer must choose a compound class. **Carrying a possessor into the verb.** Andrews’s **ōnicnochiualtocac** carries the **no-** of “my made thing” into the verb as an object that refers back to the speaker. ## Building a nominal clause from a verbal predicate

| Control | Where and when | Action and inferred purpose | Sweep disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nominalization | Predicate-nominalization Grammar group | Choose what kind of nominal expression to make from the verbal material. An agentive names a participant who performs the action. Andrews's fully nominal customary agentive **tlamatinitl** names one who habitually knows things. | Retain in this pass |
| NNC operation | Deverbal Grammar family selector | Choose which kind of nominal formation or reuse to prepare. For example, predicate nominalization derives the customary agentive **tlamatinitl** from the knowing predicate. The family selection establishes the fields required before Make. | Retain in this pass |
| Preterit source analysis | Conditional predicate-nominalization Grammar | Identify the licensed ordinary or obsolete-root analysis for the accepted verb. In the **izta-ya → iztāc** route, the predicate's analysis supplies the nominal base before **c**. | Retain in this pass |
| Spelling | Conditional predicate-nominalization Grammar | Choose the regular form or Andrews's retained spelling when both are available. In **iztāc**, the retained **ā** falls just before **c**. This choice records the written form independently of the Source analysis. | Retain in this pass |
| Agentive number realization | Conditional preterit-agentive Grammar | Select the licensed number form when the route offers one. Andrews's **micqui** illustrates **qui** after a restricted-use stem. This selector belongs to the preterit agentive group. | Retain in this pass |
| Plural agentive shape | Conditional preterit-agentive Grammar | Select **plain** or **affinity** when both are licensed. Andrews gives **tlattaqueh ~ tlātlattaqueh** ‘they are onlookers’. Both are plural. The second adds the affinity copy at the left of the stem. | Retain in this pass |
| Preterit agentive form | Conditional preterit-agentive Grammar when the lexical inventory licenses a variant | Choose the applicable ordinary, archaic **quē**, or **yauh** form with an internal possessor. In Andrews's **micquētl**, the archaic **quē** goes between **mic** and **-tl**. | Retain in this pass |
| Supplementary object activation | Conditional predicate-nominalization Grammar | Keep the object inside the nominalized predicate or specify a particular object when the construction needs one. In Andrews's **tlayōhualli quimonāhualtih**, the overt supplementary object is written first and the activated **qui-** precedes **mo-** and the stem. | Retain in this pass |
| Agentive boundary spelling | Deverbal Grammar when an absolutive preterit agentive exposes **uc** before singular **qui** or eligible plural number material | Choose **regular** to keep **uc**, or **delabialized** to write **c** immediately before the connector. Andrews’s grave-coverer agentive illustrates the eligible boundary. [Canvas and matched Owner spelling check](#spelling-an-exposed-agentive-consonant) | Retain in this pass |
| Final i at boundary | Deverbal Grammar when an exact customary-agentive parent and its intended use license a boundary variant | With **tēcuāni** prepared, choose whether its final **i** stays. Andrews’s singular possessive **itēcuān** illustrates loss after **n**. In a compound, the chosen spelling affects the join just before the matrix. [Canvas, Owner, and visibility evidence](#choosing-final-i-at-a-customary-agentive-boundary) | Retain in this pass |
| Patientive source | Deverbal Grammar for patientive formation and its compound continuations | Identify what existing material will supply the nominal stem. Andrews's customary-present patientive starts from a passive predicate and names the entity treated that way. Other patientive families use different cores. | Retain in this pass |
| Patientive from reconstructed base | Deverbal continuation picker after an exact issued type-two causative sentence when the Owner validates its reconstructed nonactive bridge | With the saved **quicochītia** sentence prepared, choose this continuation to reuse **cochī-hua**, then supply **State** and **Subject**. The runtime writes **cochi → tl**. Andrews’s **(coch)-tli-** uses a different boundary, and §25.1 explains the causative ancestry. [Canvas, runtime contrast, and controls](#reusing-a-reconstructed-base-as-a-patientive) | Retain in this pass |
| Patientive analogy | Conditional patientive Grammar with a perfective or imperfective active core | Choose the licensed passive or impersonal model for building the noun. Andrews gives passive-model **quēntli** ‘clothing’ and impersonal-model **tlapāhuaztli** ‘stew’. | Retain in this pass |
| Possessed stem / Noun ending | Conditional patientive Grammar. The renderer relabels the shell’s **Stem shape** field as **Possessed stem** for the imperfective route and **Noun ending** for root-or-stock. | Choose the licensed nounstem class for the derived noun. In Andrews's **cuīcatl**, put the sung-material stem **cuīca** before **-tl**. In **nocuīc**, possession is written at the left and the form ends with **cuīc**. The fixture supplies the noun-class value `tl-2-b-a` with the exact active **cuica** parent. The rendered selector is scoped to the current parent. The Canvas pair shows why the class matters across states. The exact public options and click path remain unverified. [Canvas §39.2](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L15219) · [Field label](../../src/ui/shell/classical_shell.mjs#L1523) · [Parent scoping](../../src/ui/rendering/nominal_construction_presentation.mjs#L6406) · [Exact active-source fixture](../../src/tests/classical_lesson39_group_15_jobs.test.js#L10) | Retain in this pass |
| Nounstem relation | Passive-core patientive Grammar when the authorized frame offers affinity | Request a plain or affinity-shaped nounstem. Andrews's **tex-tli** shows the plain structure, with the ground-material stem before **-tli**. An eligible affinity choice operates on the nominal base before the ending is written. | Retain in this pass |
| Licensed root or stock allomorph | Root-or-stock patientive Grammar when the Source inventory offers a choice | Choose a licensed realization just before the noun ending. In **cual-a-x-tli** ‘anger’, **x** comes after the stock and before **-tli**. The class of verb alone does not establish which consonant is licensed. | Retain in this pass |
| Root or stock Source analysis | Conditional Grammar for a historically ambiguous Source | Identify the direction of derivation where the Source admits both analyses. The Owner fixture records the same **zōm** stem for a deverbal patientive and a nounstem root used to form a verb. | Retain in this pass |
| Characteristic reading | Conditional characteristic-property Grammar | Specify what kind of characteristic is expressed. Andrews's **nomiyo** uses **yo** after **omi** for a bone belonging organically to the person. **Nomiuh** illustrates acquired possession in a different formation. | Retain in this pass |
| Acquired relation | Conditional perfective patientive Grammar when an ownerhood Source requires a contextual reading | Choose **family member** or **slave**, as licensed by the captured Source. Andrews analyzes the child form as **pil → huah → tli**, with the acquired-entity stem following **pil**. | Retain in this pass |
| Ownerhood matrix | Deverbal Grammar for ownerhood | Request an available **ē**, **huā**, or abundant-ownerhood matrix. Andrews contrasts **tōcāyeh**, an owner of a name, with **tōcāyoh**, an owner of abundant names. The matrix follows the name material. | Retain in this pass |
| Embed variant | Ownerhood Grammar when Source analysis supplies multiple boundary variants | Choose a licensed shape at the end of the first stem. In **tōcāyeh**, **y** belongs to the first piece at the join before **eh**. Exact availability of the variant picker for this example remains unverified. | Retain in this pass |
| Patientive referent | Impersonal-core patientive Grammar when the Source inventory requires a reading choice | With the favor verb prepared, choose whether the noun names the recipient or the favor. Andrews writes **tla-cn-ēl-i-l** for the person and **tē-icn-ēl-ī-l** for the favor. The choice affects the left-edge prefix and the inner vowel. With the exact ordinary impersonal Source tested, the Owner supplies the favor reading automatically and the renderer hides the field. [Canvas and Source comparison](#choosing-the-patientive-referent) | Retain in this pass |
| Surviving tē in double-object patientive | Passive-core patientive Grammar when the Owner allows omission of the sole surviving nonspecific human object | With Andrews’s passive loan stem **tē-(tlan-ē-uh-ti-lō)** prepared, choose **retain** to write **tē** before **tlan-ē-uh-tī-l**, or **delete** to start at **tlan**. The noun ending follows either stem. [Andrews’s loan pair and Owner eligibility](#choosing-whether-to-write-the-surviving-object) | Retain in this pass |

**Which material Patientive source chooses.** Andrews §37.8 gives five basic sources. With eligible verbal material prepared, the writer identifies which piece supplies the nounstem before choosing its ending or nominal use. The app puts this choice in Grammar even though the label says **Source**. Canvas Atoms `ACI-P378-L005-52329FC142` through `ACI-P378-L005-52329FC142-05` identify the five categories under the taxonomy Owner. | Patientive source option | Prepared material and written effect |
| --- | --- |
| passive core | With the passive grinding stem **tex-ō** prepared, the noun starts with **tex** and ends with **tli**. The nonactive suffix is removed. [Canvas passive example](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L14653) |
| impersonal core | With the impersonal cooking core prepared, the stew noun starts with **tla**, then writes **pā → hua → x → tli**. [Canvas stew contrast](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L15109) |
| perfective active core | With the cooking verb’s perfective active core prepared, choosing the impersonal analogy gives **tla → pā → hua → z → tli**. Compare the **x** at the same position in the impersonal-core form. [Canvas stew contrast](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L15109) |
| imperfective active core | With the imperfective song base **cuīca** prepared, the absolutive writes **cuīca → tl**. The possessed example writes **no → cuīc**. [Canvas song pair](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L15219) |
| root or stock | With **tō-ni** prepared, select the root-or-stock route and then an ending after **tōch**. The isolated rabbit runs below cover that click sequence and the two accepted forms. |

The renderer restricts the matrix continuation to passive or impersonal, holds the retained source family for an authorized embed continuation, and restricts an eligible ownerhood source to the perfective active core. An exact reconstructed nonactive parent or a characteristic-forming nominal input can supply a fixed family with the menu hidden. The shell also lists the preterit-agentive characteristic-property route. These are renderer observations. The rabbit sequence below establishes the corresponding typed route in the browser. **What the accepted verb supplies.** When a patientive starts from an exact Result, its binding supplies the source family. The renderer sets **Patientive source** from that binding, such as passive core, impersonal core, perfective active, or imperfective active. In the song example, the retained active verb supplies the imperfective core. **Patientive analogy** and **Stem shape** describe how the writer turns that core into the noun. The earlier source choice is carried forward when the exact binding already answers it. [Binding-to-family mapping](../../src/ui/rendering/nominal_construction_presentation.mjs#L7005) · [Canvas song example](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L15219)

**Building from a verb core before any verbal clause is written.** The renderer can pass an eligible simple verb stem and its Source facts directly to the patientive core Owner. With **nōtza** prepared, the writer chooses **Patientive source → perfective active core** and **Patientive analogy → impersonal**. For ‘I am a guest’, the new nominal subject **ni-** comes first, followed by **tla → nōtz → tli**. The Owner supplies **tla-** under the impersonal model. With **toca** prepared, **imperfective active core → passive** and plural nominal agreement give **toca → meh**. The nominal agreement belongs to the expression now being written. Both Owner cases passed with an empty Source subject and no finite verbal Result, including restoration of the exact core dependency from the construction number. These are renderer and Owner checks. Atoms `ACI-P392-L006-C53240ECC4` and `ACI-P394-L004-29AA3B459B` record the written examples. **Choosing a nonactive base before making the noun.** The patientive renderer also uses the **Nonactive formation** selector when the selected passive or impersonal source has multiple formations. It asks **Choose the nonactive Source formation** if a choice is required. With zero or one form the selector is hidden, and a sole authorized form can be supplied automatically. Andrews's **ihcuanī-lō / ihcuanī-hua** pair illustrates the writing decision: the writer keeps **ihcuanī** and chooses the formation to its right. The Lesson 20 fixture expects both bases and a required selector for the verbal case. For a patientive, the selected formation is input to the noun-building rule. Which letters survive is determined by that rule. This example establishes the verbal alternatives. Public use of this particular pair in the patientive picker remains unverified. The nominal ending follows the stem in either case. The documented giving fixture covers the same left-edge decision with **tē-mac** and **mac**. ### Choosing the patientive referent

Andrews gives two ways to turn the favor verb into a noun. **Human · regular tla** puts **tla** before **cn-ēl-i-l** for the person receiving the favor. **Nonhuman or abstract · anomalous tē** puts **tē** before **icn-ēl-ī-l** for the favor itself. The Owner supplies the inner vowel differences. Atoms `ACI-P388-L025-26CE20A73E-03` and `ACI-P388-L027-B3D13389A7` record these readings. The distinct **human · exceptional tē** option belongs to the **huīca** profile, where Andrews gives **tē → huica → l → li** ‘servant or companion’ alongside the usual **tla → huica → l → li**. Atom `ACI-P388-L007-F74EE8A13C` records this exceptional human formation. ### Reusing a reconstructed base as a patientive

**Written order and evidence.** The writer starts with an issued type-two causative sentence and chooses **Patientive from reconstructed base**, then supplies the new noun’s State and subject. The recovered stem goes before the new nominal ending. Andrews §25.1 explains why a causative can preserve an otherwise unattested nonactive base. Atoms `ACI-P210-L004-A6D2089C00` and `ACI-P210-L004-FC4B188470` record that explanation. In the separate **nixcohtiyān** example, Atom `ACI-P475-L026-62B0535FD5-08` records the reconstructed **ix-co-h** patientive foundation written after **n** and before **ti-yā-n**. This clarifies the position of recovered material. The dedicated continuation verifies the issued sentence and its selected derivational bridge. The writer chooses to reuse the recorded analysis. The bridge supplies the nonactive base, and the Owner requires impersonal analogy. Andrews gives the same derivational chain for the sleeping verb, **cochi → cochi-hua → tē-(cochi-tiā)**. Atom `ACI-P211-L002-9E701CC58F` identifies that example. In the written causative, the participant marker precedes the derived stem. ### Choosing final i at a customary agentive boundary

**Where final i is decided.** A customary form such as **tēcuāni** keeps its final vowel in the ordinary standalone build tested by the fixture. The destination of that material can create a new choice later. Andrews explicitly describes final **i** loss in the singular possessive context and optional shortening before **tzin** in the personal-name example above. For the singular possessive, Andrews’s **itēcuān** writes **i → tē → cuā → n**. The writer has the customary base **tēcuāni**, then chooses the possessive use and the licensed loss at the far right. Atom `ACI-P355-L034-7E400F7E4C` records the exact form. In the current boundary suite, the bound-material case passed. The other four cases stopped before their assertions at the same missing function extraction. Their fixture loads the former rendering module, while the implementation is in the nominal construction presenter. Standalone use hid the field and reset the selection to **preserve**. Licensed possessive use offered **preserve** and **drop-possessive-singular**. The exact compound parent offered **preserve** and **drop-compound**, kept the selected loss for the same parent, and reset it after that parent was removed. The nominal compound applies the choice to the retained or additionally supplied constituent as appropriate to its role. The inspected collector paths then pass the constituent carrying its exact Result and final-i bridge to the Owner. | Action formation | Conditional deverbal-action Grammar | Choose among the offered active-action, potential-patient, and impersonal general-action routes. The choice tells the application what kind of noun the writer is trying to form. | Retain in this pass |

| Compound matrix stem | Action noun continued into a nominal or verbal compound | Supply the stem that follows the saved action. In **tlanamaquilizcalli**, **cal** follows the selling action. In **chōquiliztzahtzi**, **tzahtzi** follows the weeping action. | Retain in this pass |
| Matrix noun class / Matrix verb class | Respective nominal and verbal continuation branches | Identify the class of the second stem. | Embed–patientive relation | Same continuation | Choose how the first stem relates to the patientive. In **āhuictli**, the water material expresses where the carried implement is for use. | Retain in this pass |
| Compound target | Patientive embed continuation | Decide whether the patientive goes before a nominal or verbal matrix. Andrews's **tlacualcalli** puts the food stem before **cal** ‘house’. In **cecmiqui**, the patientive meaning ‘coldness’ comes before **miqui** ‘die’. | Retain in this pass |
| Characteristic yō in the embed | Patientive embed continuation with authorized omission, or ownerhood with multiple characteristic forms | Keep the full characteristic formation or omit its matrix while carrying its meaning into the compound. In Andrews's heart example, **yōl-lō** and **yōl** can each precede **chic-ā-hu-a** with the sense ‘strengthen oneself in the heart’. | Retain in this pass |
| Compound matrix stem | Patientive embed continuation after selecting the target | Supply the piece that follows the patientive. For the nominal **tlacualcalli** it is **cal**, while in verbal **cecmiqui** it is **miqui**. | Retain in this pass |
| Matrix noun class | Nominal arm of patientive embed continuation | Identify the class of the nounstem that governs the compound. In **tlacualcalli**, **cal** comes after **tlacual** and supplies the class associated with the final **-li**. | Retain in this pass |

## Choosing direction inside a verbal clause

| Control | Where and when | Action and inferred purpose | Sweep disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Directional / locative | Grammar, when the verbal route exposes direction | Select **none**, **on** for distance, or **huāl** for proximity. This lets the writer say where an action takes place or which way movement goes relative to the speaker. | Retain in this pass |
| Optional directional contraction | Native verbal Grammar under **Verb formation** when the displayed machinery frame authorizes the directional **itta** contraction context | Choose **Ordinary** or **Rare contraction** where Andrews licenses the contracted form. It lets the writer choose a realization of the direction they already selected. Andrews's example contrasts **noconitta** and **nocotta**. | Retain in this pass |

**Composition on paper.** In Andrews's **huālcholoa**, the direction comes before the intransitive stem. Compare **tiquimonittayah**, where the specific object precedes **on**. The same semantic choice occupies different written positions according to the clause's valence. In **Grammar**, choose **Make a verb clause**, open **Mood and tense** and **Verb formation**, set subject person to **first** and tense to **present**, then set **Directional / locative → on**. **Make Result** accepted **Noconitta** with Linear **#no-0+c-0+on(itt-a)0+0-0#**. The **Optional directional contraction** select was mounted, hidden, disabled, and set to **Ordinary** both before Make and after returning to Grammar. This public route verifies the ordinary written join and shows where the rare option was inaccessible. The runtime evidence above establishes **nocotta** for the licensed rare choice. | Degree | Conditional Adverbial grammar | Choose how an eligible nominal expression takes on an adverbial function when its source licenses both degrees. In Andrews’s **Zan tequitl ōnitlacuah, niman ōniyah**, the writer puts **Zan tequitl** before **ōnitlacuah**. First-degree adverbialization leaves the shape of the subject pronoun intact. Second degree changes the connector inside the nominal clause to the silent form. Thus, the selected degree can affect material inside a prepared expression before the writer continues to the right. The lexical record for **tequitl** supplies first degree alone, so this example explains the distinction without demonstrating a selectable Degree field. The renderer shows **Degree** with multiple authorized values, and the evaluator accepts a sole licensed degree without a choice. Atoms `ACI-P445-L018-DDCC756DD0`, `ACI-P445-L020-60E731B56F`, and `ACI-P445-L029-7195896B68` record the distinction and its applicability. A separate authorization check and any matching clause binding block determine whether the button is enabled. | Request the whole expression. The current layout marks this action as a duplicate when **Make Result** serves the active clause workflow. | Retain in this pass |

**Choosing a relation before both pieces are ready.** The **Relation** selector can keep a route selectable when the controller reports a missing prerequisite and names a capture role that can supply it. The option includes the available recovery text. Incompatible options are disabled. If the selected relation has several roles for the current Result and no role can be carried forward, Grammar asks **Choose a Result role for this relation**. For **Huel xontlachiye.**, the observed route uses **Xontlachiye.** as principal and retrieves **Huel.** as the missing adjoined Result. This is preparing the pieces in a different order from the written line. The selector rules are from code. The role and retrieval sequence is recorded in the watch-command replay, which did not exercise every type of disabled option. **When Relation choices appear.** After the writer selects **Relation**, the shared panel renders other choices from the current decision contract once the required pieces are captured. A decision that determines which pieces are needed can appear earlier. **Comparison construction** is an example. The Owner exposes the route choice before it derives the required roles from that choice. This lets the writer specify the intended comparison before retrieving the appropriate pieces, even though those pieces may later be written in a different order. The select starts with **Choose [label]**, disabled when the decision is required. The option list preserves the controller’s availability and recovery information. Unavailable choices are disabled except for a **Relation** with a recoverable missing capture. See the comparison examples for where each chosen relation takes effect in the writing. **How to tell which piece is required.** The shared panel uses two different signals. **Capture as…** becomes actionable when the current Result and its Source projection are ready. The click asks the controller to accept the Result in that role. **Determined structure** draws its **required captures** list from the active decision contract. In **Cāmpa mochān?**, that list can identify the three participating slots even though the generic capture area also offers a fourth button. The list describes the slots required for composition, including any already filled. The cards record which Results actually occupy those slots. A filled card shows **Captured canonical Result**, its unit, and its written form. An empty marker, dependent, or supplement card says **Optional** based on the slot name. The active contract can require that same slot. For the rain sequence, the third conjunct uses the dependent slot, so its empty card’s generic caption gives weaker guidance than the contract about whether the writer still needs to supply the third event. Those cards require both an eligible saved identity and a usable structure projection. The native **Add [role] Result** picker can still list an eligible identity whose card projection is missing. For the **Petoloh** example, the writer uses the slot picker to supply the name after **Ōquittac**. History search instead lets the writer return to the saved name build itself. The difference in candidate scope follows the renderer. The observed attachment used the visible card. **When the search starts over.** **Find Results** is tied to the current Source, operation, binding, and open role. Changing one of those clears the search when a new compatible list is shown. For example, in the two calendar routes the writer searches for a numeral when starting from **Calli**, or a day sign when starting from **Cē**. Either route writes **Cē → Calli**. The picker search serves the missing role, and its reset follows that role even when the final line stays the same. The role-specific pickers and accepted lines were observed in Chrome. The reset condition is from the renderer. [Search context and reset](../../src/ui/composition/candidate_design.mjs#L78) · [Calendar browser sequences](#writing-a-calendar-date)

**When a displayed card has gone stale.** Clicking a card rechecks the current Source, binding, operation, role, and enabled native option. The handler also compares the saved Result’s exact identity and asks the current picker whether it still qualifies. If the draft changes before the click reaches the handler, an obsolete card cannot replace the selected piece. For the writer completing **Ōquittac Petoloh**, this keeps the next piece tied to the current draft’s open role. The card only selects an eligible item. The separate **Use this Result** action supplies it. Andrews separately gives a head-first example without **in**, **Centetl cahciqueh tōtōtl nextic.** For the writer, the order choice identifies which piece to put before the intervening clause, and the marker choice determines whether the modifier has an explicit introduction where the construction licenses it. ### Joining nouns in a lexical conjunction

| Control | Where and when | Action and inferred purpose | Sweep disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lexical relation | Relation choices after both constituents of a lexical conjunction are captured | Identify the intended interpretation of the pair. Andrews uses **mītl** and **tetl** in the account of arrows and rocks falling on the Spaniards. | Retain in this pass |
| in distribution | Same relation choices | Choose how the adjunctor is distributed across the ordered constituents. **In mītl in tetl** writes one **in** before each noun. | Retain in this pass |
| State realization | Same relation choices | Specify the licensed state realization of the joined expression. The controller carries this choice separately from marker placement. | Retain in this pass |

**Writing the joined nouns.** The retained §57.1 browser run made **Mītl.** and **Tetl.** separately and joined them before using the pair in the larger sentence. On paper, the local order is **in → mītl → in → tetl**. The controller exposes decisions for the two captured inputs. Address replay retained the ordered nouns, marker distribution, and state realization. This is evidence for the marked route used in that run. The renderer supplies the field names above. The native renderer derives the option captions from the Owner values, as listed below. [Rendered labels](../../src/ui/rendering/nominal_construction_presentation.mjs#L12429) · [Canvas §57.1](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L24719) · [Controller decisions](../../src/owner/classical/clause_relation_organ.mjs#L2996) · [Retained lexical conjunction replay](andrews-grammar-os-topology-map.md#L1918) · [Blank-workspace run](andrews-grammar-os-topology-map.md#L1926)

**Three choices for the same pair.** The §57.1 fixture captures **mītl** and **tetl**, then requests the lexical type `bread-and-butter`, distribution `in-before-each`, and state realization `conjoined-stems`. With **mītl** and **tetl** already captured, the lexical type treats them as the paired subject of the falling clause. Atom `ACI-P623-L015-06EEB1662E` records their placement together after **Onhuetzi** and before **in īmpan Españoles**. The distribution determines where **in** is written, once directly before each noun. The state choice describes how the stems are realized within the conjunction. The replay evidence preserves all three coordinates, so the twice-written **in** is evidence of the selected distribution, while the retained state and type come from the captured analysis. The current renderer formats those values as **Bread and butter**, **In before each**, and **Conjoined stems**. The other values in the same menus render as **Lord and master**, **None**, **In before left only**, and **Compound handoff**. **How the shared capture panel names the pieces.** The comparison route supplies slot names to **Capture as [slot]**. Across the 23 current layouts, the names are **source**, **principal**, **adjoined**, **comparand**, **standard**, **topic**, **dimension**, **point**, **predicate**, **similarityClause**, **headClause**, **leftClause**, **rightClause**, **baseClause**, **superiorClause**, and **degreeClause**. The controller separately identifies the required slots. For example, **dimension** is part of the equality layout, while the bull fixture only needs the comparand and standard. In the size fixture, **Standard** occupies the controller’s principal slot and is captured first. The accepted line puts the **Comparand** first and writes the standard after **ixquich in**. This lets the writer revisit the opening **in → tlā** without having to enter its filled slots twice when using the preset. These are renderer and handler findings. ### Extending a particle sequence

**Extending a particle sequence from the left.** Andrews gives **in tlā** and **in tlā zan**. The writer can start with **in → tlā** and extend it with **zan** at the right edge where the sequence permits. The consolidated **Particles** picker presents a prepared sequence as one selection when available. Its renderer marks already filled sequence slots as covered and leaves a licensed unfilled **Next particle** choice visible. To adjust the individual pieces, selecting the first particle again restarts the underlying sequence builder. The underlying builder computes each slot from the selected prefix. Selecting a later slot keeps the earlier segments, replaces the chosen segment, and drops any later segments so they can be chosen again. For the writer building this opener piece by piece, the planned action sequence is **Particles → in → Next particle: tlā → Next particle: zan**, in the same order as the written opener. Selecting the prepared **in tlā zan** preset combines those choices into one. These sequences come from the builder and compact renderer. The exact step-by-step sequence remains unobserved in the browser. Atom `ACI-P059-L018-19FD991827` gives the last-member attachment rule, `ACI-P059-L021-7061D7CA2C` records scope over the entire sequence, and `ACI-P059-L026-BB2A070E1D` records the particular written form. The writer chooses honorific treatment. The grammar puts **-tzin** on **zo**. The Owner fixture checks typed particle inputs and final-member attachment. The button labels and enablement come from the renderer. A public click sequence for this collocation remains unverified. **Canvas and writing order.** Andrews §3.1 distinguishes dependent particles with different written positions. **ō** joins to what follows, while vocative **é** is written after the nominal clause. Thus the picker identifies the particle and the construction determines its position. For a collocation such as **in tlā**, the ordered segments are the pieces the writer expects to see. The shell's separate singular **Particle** selector is marked internal and hidden. The saved-Result **In** journey under Purpose above is a separate path from this sentence particle picker. ## Rephrasing a clause with a more specific object

| Control | Where and when | Action and inferred purpose | Sweep disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Rephrasive | Grammar after capturing the two conjuncts | Identify the second clause as a rephrasing of the first. | Retain in this pass |
| Nonspecific–specific object | Conditional rephrasing choice | Specify what becomes more specific. In Andrews's drum example, the first clause describes drumming and the second identifies the drum. | Retain in this pass |
| No apposition / comma | Conditional decisions recorded in the public route | Keep the conjuncts in the attested relation and write the comma at their boundary. | Retain in this pass |
| Capture as first conjunct / second conjunct / third conjunct | Shared clause-composition panel for parallel structure and conjunction families, when a compatible current Result can fill the role | Supply each prepared clause to its position in the current group. In Andrews’s rain example the third event clause is **ihcuāc mozcalia**. | Retain in this pass |
| Parallel structure (parallel type) | Parallel structure decisions after capturing the first two expressions | Choose whether the following expression restates the same content, advances to new content in a similar form, or does both. Andrews’s drum example restates the action. His rain example moves from awakening to moving to reviving. | Retain in this pass |
| Rephrasing axis | Rephrasive or combined parallel structure where the Owner can identify a licensed grammatical contrast | Say how the second piece restates the first. The drum example moves from an unspecified thing being struck to a specified drum. | Retain in this pass |
| Appositive type | Parallel structure decisions | Choose whether the following material clarifies or summarizes the preceding material, or select **none**. In Andrews’s kitchenware example the named utensils come first, followed by the summary **mochi**. | Retain in this pass |
| Punctuation between clauses | Parallel structure after the pieces are captured | Choose the mark at the joint. The kitchenware fixture places a dash between the list and **mochi**, which begins the summary. | Retain in this pass |

**Why the rephrasing choice exists.** Andrews describes restating the same content in a slightly different form. Atom `ACI-P571-L013-53947C9125` assigns that definition to the rephrasing Owner. Atom `ACI-P571-L016-49E1F2286E-02` assigns the nonspecific-to-specific object pattern to the grammatical variants Owner. Atom `ACI-P571-L031-4B4ECA2814` records **Tlatzotzona, quitzotzona in īhuēhuēuh.** as the written example. The writer begins with the general action and then names what was struck. The **Rephrasing axis** choice records that relationship between two pieces the writer has already prepared. **Writing the next event in the same pattern.** Andrews’s rain sentence begins **In ihcuāc cuacualaca quiyahuitl**, then writes **ihcuāc ihza → ihcuāc moholīnia → ihcuāc mozcalia**, with commas between the clauses. Each repeated **ihcuāc** starts a clause about a new event. The Owner fixture prepares those three event clauses separately, sets **Parallel structure → Progressive**, **Appositive type → None**, and **Punctuation between clauses → Comma**, then adds the opening time clause. It verifies four independently issued instances of **ihcuāc** in the exact inputs. The writer chooses and supplies the next event. The repeated opening belongs to the prepared clauses, and the progressive relation joins them. This is controller evidence. The exact public progressive path remains unverified. ## Writing around an introductory particle

| Control | Where and when | Action and inferred purpose | Sweep disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Introductory | Grammar, in the sentence choices | Choose the opening particle or collocation where licensed. In Andrews's **Mā cuēl mocuiltōno!**, **mā** introduces the wish. | Retain in this pass |
| Before introductory | Grammar, in the sentence choices | Place a preface before the introducer. Andrews explains that **ihyo** can precede the introductory particle to express a fervent wish. | Retain in this pass |
| After introductory | Grammar, in the sentence choices | Choose material immediately after the introducer. Andrews gives **Mā cuēl mocuiltōno!** and **Mā ye cuēl xiccaquicān!** as examples of intensifying a wish. | Retain in this pass |

**Writing order and interaction.** The example starts **mā → cuēl → mocuiltōno → !**. The shell declares **Introductory** before **Before introductory**, so the code lists those choices in a different order from the written sentence. The labels can also be read as instructions for revising an opener already chosen. The composer stores the after-introductory modifier separately. In a fresh Chrome Analysis session, type **cochi**, select Class **B**, apply Source, then choose **Grammar → Make a verb clause → Mood and tense → optative** and open **Sentence choices**. **Introductory** had **mā** set. All three native fields were mounted but invisible, including after the disclosure opened. The **Before introductory** field had a hidden label and was inside a hidden authority group. The visible **Make Result** accepted **Mā nicochi.**, with **mā** before the verbal clause in Analysis. That verifies the default opener on this route. Selecting **ihyo** and **cuēl** remained unavailable in the tested draft. [Isolated optative browser check](/tmp/ui-intent-wish-public-make.json)

[Canvas wishes and the preface](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L3628) · [Three control definitions](../../src/ui/shell/classical_shell.mjs#L4529) · [Composer choice capture](../../src/ui/composer/composer.mjs#L4955)

**When the fields appear.** The Result-surface renderer requires the corresponding sentence capability for each field. **Before introductory** and **After introductory** also require an active introducer. In a nonpast second-person optative, **Introductory** can offer **none**. Other optatives in this contract require **mā**, **tlā**, or **in tlā** and use **mā** as the fallback. With an introducer active, the optative preface options include **ihyo**, with **ye** offered for **tlā**. The following modifier options depend on the introducer and tense. Thus a writer with **Mā** already staged can choose **cuēl** as the next written piece, or choose **ihyo** to revise the beginning. A readout beside the three existing fields could show **Ihyo → mā → cuēl** in written order before Make. The continuation presenter separately recalculates these controls for a verbal application or for a sentence operation with an eligible continuation context. It shows a particle field when that draft offers a value other than **none**. The gate and option rules are source evidence. The readout is a design inference. It recalculates dependent options and reads the displayed fallbacks before staging the revised request. The writer's available choices come from that draft. In the observed optative and continuation states, the missing step is reaching the licensed fields. A change to their placement or visibility would use the existing request path. With a prepared wish, the writer can revise its opening to **Ihyo → mā** or continue from **Mā → cuēl**. ### Choosing how to use a sentence

| Control | Where and when | Action and inferred purpose | Sweep disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sentence use (optative) | Conditional verbal sentence Grammar | Specify wish, command, or exhortation when the route offers the choice. In Andrews's wish **Mā tlapāca.**, the introductory **mā** comes before the optative clause. | Retain in this pass |
| Source meaning | Included-possessor denominal Grammar when the recognized meaning is unresolved | Identify a proxy or recompense Source. In Andrews's recompense example **molhuilti**, the included possessor comes before the recompense material and verbal **ti** follows it. | Retain in this pass |
| Sentence use (denominal exclamation) | Included-possessor denominal Grammar for an eligible preterit recompense form | Choose the idiomatic exclamation. In **Ōimilhuiltic!**, antecessive material goes first, and the exclamation mark follows the preterit form. | Retain in this pass |

**Effect on the expression.** The optative choice concerns what the writer is doing with an already identified clause. The denominal checkbox has a narrower lexical and tense condition. The renderer exposes it for recompense with preterit selected and supplies required exclamatory use separately for Sources that demand it. Andrews's recompense example motivates the dedicated control. The exact browser sequences for these choices remain unverified. **When Andrews determines the sentence use.** In §54.3, the recompense examples include present **molhuilti** and future **tolhuiltiz**, while **Ōimilhuiltic!** illustrates an idiomatic preterit exclamation. By contrast, Andrews requires preterit and exclamation for the misfortune type, as in **Ōnotlahuēliltic!**. On paper the misfortune example starts with **ō**, puts the included possessor before the rest of the verbal stem, and ends with **!**. The renderer narrows Tense to the required value and supplies the exclamation without offering the optional recompense checkbox. The writer supplies the appropriate Source and possessor. The Source determines the sentence conditions in this branch. Four focused UI checks stopped at fixture setup because the extraction helper could not find the nominal-control function. Current evidence for availability comes from the renderer and Canvas, with the browser sequence unverified. ## Turning a sentence into a question

| Control | Where and when | Action and inferred purpose | Sweep disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sentence | Grammar sentence-surface selector, where offered | Choose **statement**, **question**, or **exclamation**. With **Ahchōca** already written, asking a yes/no question by intonation puts **?** at the right edge in place of the period. | Keep the sentence view |
| Question | Conditional sentence Grammar selector, hidden in the base shell | Choose **Intonation** or **Cuix**. The latter puts an explicit question particle at the beginning. | Retain in this pass |
| Adjunctor in | Conditional pronominal NNC Grammar | Identify a following dependent clause with separate **in**, or choose an elliptical fused form where licensed. Starting with **āc**, put **in** after it as a separate piece when the dependent clause follows. In elliptical **Āquin?** or **Āqui?**, the fused material becomes part of the interrogative word. | Retain in this pass |

**Compound matrix.** In Grammar for an exact typed **cā** Source, the renderer generates **Compound matrix** when the pronominal binding supplies an available matrix option. Andrews gives three ways to continue after **cā** in §16.4.3. Choose **tl-eh** to write **cā → tleh → ?**, **tl-e-in** to write **cā → tlein → ?**, or **tl-eh-huā** to write **cā → tlehhuā → tl → ?**. The binding also offers **none** for plain **cā**. The writer chooses which matrix to add at the right edge. The Owner supplies the associated number form. Changing the matrix clears previous number and predicate-pluralization choices before the draft is restaged. Atom `ACI-P144-L039-6326744D09` records the licensed matrices. All eight focused Owner cases passed, including the exact three forms and rejection of arbitrary matrices. The public order of clicks for the generated selector remains unverified. [Canvas §16.4.3](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L5529) · [Atom ledger](../ANDREWS_ATOM_LEDGER.json) · [Selector condition](../../src/ui/rendering/owner_journey_presentation.mjs#L574) · [Change handler](../../src/ui/rendering/owner_journey_presentation.mjs#L759) · [Focused fixture](../../src/tests/pronominal_interrogative_compound_source.test.mjs#L35)

**Typed Source label and options.** In a typed pronominal NNC operation plan, the generated selector keeps the native name **Adjunctor in**. It uses the native wording **dependent clause, separate in** and **elliptical tlein**, **elliptical tlei**, **elliptical tlen**, **elliptical āquin**, or **elliptical aqui** when the exact binding offers those values. The captions come from the native field. The displayed options come from the current binding. For a writer starting with **tleh**, the first caption signals that **in** goes next and another clause must follow it. The elliptical captions name forms that can finish the question word. This is a shell and renderer cross-check. [Native captions](../../src/ui/shell/classical_shell.mjs#L3610) · [Generated caption mapping](../../src/ui/rendering/owner_journey_presentation.mjs#L585)

**Use principal clause.** When **Adjunctor in** requests a following dependent clause that has yet to be supplied, the workbench can show **Use principal clause** next to the editable field. It stages the bare question word from the same Source. The disabled **Add a dependent clause** caption belongs to **Make Result** in the incomplete state. After using the recovery action, the writer makes the principal, opens **Combine Results**, and supplies the material that follows **in**. This supports Andrews’s sequence **tleh → in → dependent clause**. The renderer can keep **Add a dependent clause** disabled while the Adjunctor field is remounting and the recovery button is temporarily absent. It attaches **Use principal clause** only beside a visible, enabled field for the current binding. **Choosing the first letter of the final pronoun.** Andrews permits **eh → yeh** and **ehhuātl → yehhuātl**. The controller supplies **Default** and **Y-initial**, and the exact fixture successfully changed both short and long prepared collocations to their y-initial forms. The role of the selector is to realize a pronoun that the construction already contains. Choosing a collocation with or without a pronoun is a separate choice. Where the final pronoun is present, option text showing the actual pair, such as **eh / yeh**, could make the writing choice clearer. The contract records the choice, but composition blocks it with `exclamatory-personal-pronoun-variant-not-licensed`. The same choice yields **Mā cuēl yeh!** and **Mā cuēl yehhuātl!** when those exact prepared expressions contain a pronoun. ### Writing a condition

| Control | Where and when | Action and inferred purpose | Sweep disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Relation profile (condition) | Clause adverbial adjunction when the captured pair leaves a condition profile choice | Identify the licensed open or hypothetical construction. Andrews's **Itlah nimitzmacaz in tlā catleh xiquihto.** expresses an open condition. | Retain in this pass |
| Clause order (condition) | Conditional clause-relation choices for a condition | Place the condition before or after the principal where the construction licenses it. In the cited example the offer comes first and the condition follows it. | Retain in this pass |
| Optional marker Result (Condition) | Shared particle selector when the condition relation and captures admit an independent marker | Supply the licensed introducer. In the cited example **in tlā** comes immediately before **catleh xiquihto**. | Retain in this pass |

**Writing the condition at the joint.** The reader encounters **Itlah nimitzmacaz → in tlā → catleh xiquihto → period**. The exact Owner fixture builds in a different order. It first builds the offer, then joins **catleh** to **xiquihto** with the issued **in tlā ca** marker to make **In tlā catleh xiquihto.** Finally it attaches that whole condition after the offer with no separate marker in the outer request. The final sentence therefore writes **in tlā** at the join even though the fixture supplied the marker during preparation of the condition. This is an Owner build sequence. The ordinary public click sequence for the complete sentence remains unverified. [Canvas condition example](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L21550) · [Profile decision](../../src/owner/classical/clause_relation_organ.mjs#L6351) · [Exact condition fixture](../../src/tests/reader_50_7_open_condition_itlah_nimitzmacaz.test.mjs)

**When “Optional” appears on a required step.** The shared picker uses the caption **Optional marker Result** for Condition and starts with **No marker Result selected**. The controller can still require an introducer for the captured condition. In Andrews's written offer, **in tlā** goes immediately after **Itlah nimitzmacaz**. The exact fixture supplies it inside the condition before the outer join, so that join does not establish a required marker prompt. A clearer caption in a draft whose Owner availability lists a missing marker would be **Choose the condition introducer**. If the captured adjunct already carries an Owner-recognized conditional cue, the controller can accept Condition without a separately supplied marker. In that state the prompt should follow the existing eligibility rather than request a second introducer. The current evidence pairs the shared renderer caption with the controller's missing-marker behavior. The exact public Condition draft remains to be checked before treating the wording as an observed usability issue. **Canvas and Owner corroboration.** Atom `ACI-P547-L010-65F3A8D1B8` records the exact offer-first example. Atom `ACI-P547-L008-0452EAEECA-02` assigns the uncertainty associated with a nonpast optative in the conditional adjunct to the condition Owner. That uncertainty concerns the clause the writer has prepared. The outer relation uses the captured clause and its existing opening, while the profile decision appears when the Owner leaves multiple selectable profiles. Andrews's **In tlā nel cencah āc tehhuātl, ahmō huel ticchīhuaz** writes **in tlā nel** before the conceded clause. | Retain in this pass |
| Optional marker Result (concession) | Shared clause-relation picker when both clauses are captured and marker options are available | Choose **in tlā nel** to open the conceded clause. Here the introducer is the first thing the writer puts on paper. | Retain in this pass |

On paper the order is **In tlā nel → cencah āc tehhuātl → comma → ahmō huel ticchīhuaz**. The positive opening **in tlā nel** and the negative opening **in tlā canel (mō)** express different things about the conceded situation. | Control | Where and when | Action and inferred purpose | Sweep disposition |

In **Calaquih in tēmictizqueh.**, the writer finishes **Calaquih**, writes **in**, and then supplies the purpose clause. The exact **In** Result already carries the adjunctor analysis. The writer can infer the finished order by reading across those fields. The snapshot covers the Grammar region and shows no single composed line there before Make. The renderer mounts its local execution button after the required captures are ready and separately gates whether it can be pressed. For **Calaquih → in → tēmictizqueh**, these signals answer different questions: which pieces to bring in, where each goes on paper, and whether the draft is ready to make. ## Writing a report introduced by quil

| Control | Where and when | Action and inferred purpose | Sweep disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Rumored report | Clause-relation choices under Speech and address | Report something as hearsay. The fixed **quil** goes first, as in **Quil in ozomahtin quihuālihnecuih in pōctli.** | Retain in this pass |
| Capture as principal / reported clause | Capture actions for this relation | Supply the issued **quil** and the material being reported as separate Results. The reported material goes to the right of the opener. | Retain in this pass |
| Reported clause adjunctor | Rumored report decision | Choose **in** or **none**. In the monkeys example the first **in** follows **Quil** and introduces the report. The later **in pōctli** is inside the reported material. | Retain in this pass |
| Rumor particle mach | Rumored report decision | Choose whether to include **mach**. In **Quil mach mō yahqueh.**, it follows **quil**. The Owner requires **mach** and a selection of **none** for the adjunctor when the captured report has the subordinate-negative obligation illustrated by this example. | Retain in this pass |
| quil + mach boundary | When **mach** is selected | Choose **separate** or **fused**. The opening reads **Quil mach** or **Quilmach** before the same reported words. | Retain in this pass |

**From prepared clauses to written order.** Making the report requires two captures. The controller can issue the adjunctor and particle decisions while those captures are pending. The shared renderer waits for the required captures to show them. In the negative example the page reads **Quil → mach → mō yahqueh → period**. Andrews describes traditional solid spelling, and the Owner fixture asserts both spellings of this opener. The separate optional-adjunctor fixture passed in the current runtime. With the same captured inputs, it produced **Quil cuāuhtli.** and **Quil in cuāuhtli.** The added **in** goes at the start of the reported material, immediately after **Quil**. These are code and runtime evidence. The exact public labels and click sequence remain unverified. [Canvas §19.5](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L6677) · [Capture label](../../src/ui/rendering/clause_relation_presentation.mjs#L1235) · [Owner decision contract](../../src/owner/classical/clause_relation_organ.mjs#L4312) · [Optional adjunctor fixture](../../src/tests/reader_report_sentence.test.mjs#L9) · [Negative report and fusion fixture](../../src/tests/reader_44_5_complete_evidence.test.mjs#L1126)

**A choice that becomes a requirement.** The controller offers **Reported clause adjunctor** and **Rumor particle mach** for this route, then adds **quil + mach boundary** after **present** is selected. When the exact captured subordinate negative needs a governing report, the controller still builds the selectors and diagnoses a request that omits **mach** or includes the adjunctor. In **Quil mach mō yahqueh.**, the writer therefore has a spelling choice at the join between **quil** and **mach**. **What the next-step status tells the writer.** After an exact Result is continued, the operation plan can say to choose an operation, decide how to use the Result, add a missing piece, or make the draft. The organizer can suppress routine messages that repeat a stage cue or an enabled action. The remaining work was to supply **Huel**, which goes to the left of the already prepared command. The message mapping and suppression rule come from the renderer. **What Reset choices can restore.** The reset baseline belongs to the current input, operation, and binding. It records the first observed value for each tracked Grammar field in that context. Reset can restore an earlier value while the field remains editable and the earlier option remains available. It sends each restoration through the field’s ordinary change handler, and stops if a change moves the editor to another input, operation, or binding. The pending count and the reset baseline have different lifetimes. Accepting a new Result in the same draft context resets the pending count’s baseline. Reset choices still uses the first values seen in that context. In the negative and antecessive snapshot, Reset was disabled even with both selections visible. That is a recorded button state, while the tracker code supplies the rule for deciding when a reset is available. The **Pending choices** count can also include the Result-local **Order** field during a supported reorder; that field has its own edit handler. This matters when revising the page: returning to an earlier clause-order choice changes the draft, while **Undo** can return to a previously accepted build. Three focused reset tests passed, covering an eligible restore, an Owner-fixed field, and a withdrawn option. ### Optional study controls

These controls serve an invited observation session. The shell and recorder code supply their intent and conditions. The regular replay snapshot omitted the recorder controls. No recording was started for this inventory.

| Control | Where and when | Action and inferred purpose | Sweep disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Diagnostics / Advanced | Workbench support disclosure when exposed. The loaded organization uses **Diagnostics** for the shell’s **Advanced** caption. | Inspect diagnostics and reach recorder settings in an eligible session. | Retain in this pass |
| Set up private recording | Private play study entry, when manufacturer mode enables the recorder | Open recording setup. | Retain in this pass |
| Everyone being observed agreed. | Recorder setup, before recording | Confirm that the participants consented. The checkbox is disabled while the recorder loads or records. | Retain in this pass |
| Start recording | Recorder setup after consent, when off or after an error | Start observing the session. | Retain in this pass |
| Stop | Recorder controls during recording | End observation and prepare the session report. | Retain in this pass |
| Download locally | Recorder after Stop, enabled when at least one event is ready | Save the masked session report as a local JSON file. | Retain in this pass |
| Discard | Recorder in loading, recording, stopped, or error state | Clear the session data and reset consent. During loading it cancels the pending start. During recording it also stops capture. | Retain in this pass |
| Baby joy / Baby boredom | **How did play feel?**, when manufacturer play observation is active | Mark the observed response for the child audience. | Retain in this pass |
| Parent joy / Parent concern | Same observation group | Mark the observed response for the parent audience. | Retain in this pass |

The recorder is an optional observation tool. Its entry is hidden outside a manufacturer-mode session. In an eligible session, **Set up private recording** opens the controls and focuses the consent checkbox. After consent, **Start recording** can begin an in-tab masked recording. **Stop** ends it, and a stopped recording with events enables **Download locally**. The download handler writes a timestamped `grammar-os-private-play-*.json` file. The focused recorder test passed its simulated consent, masking, and local report workflow. This inventory used no live recording. ## Revisiting earlier builds

These controls provide access to earlier versions and reusable pieces. Canvas gives grammatical roles to the pieces in the resulting expression. Selecting an item in history is an interface action and does not set its written position.

| Control | Where and when | Action and inferred purpose | Sweep disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your builds | History disclosure | Expand or collapse the saved-build tools. | Retain in this pass |
| Build · Build to work with | History when the saved-build presentation is active. The underlying **Selected build** field is hidden in this presentation. | Pick the saved page to work from. This establishes which whole and which constituent buttons History offers. | Retain in this pass |
| Find builds | Beside Build. Disabled with that selector. | Filter the saved-build list by its labels while retaining the selected entry. | Retain in this pass |
| Whole sentence / constituent buttons | **Which part to work with**, after a build is selected | Choose the whole expression or an exact saved piece. A part without an unambiguous saved build is disabled. The caption shows the written form if available. | Retain in this pass |
| Use [build] | Per-build shortcut in History | Restore the exact saved Result as Source in one action. | Retain in this pass |
| Use [build] + last route | Per-build shortcut when an operation was selected | Restore that Result and try to stage the operation selected in the workbench before the click, along with the supported choices listed below. The writer still presses **Make Result** to accept the next expression. | Retain in this pass |
| Use as Source / Edit Writing Source | History action for an eligible whole or part. The second label applies to an accepted writing Source. | Carry the chosen saved expression into a new build or return to its writing entry. | Retain in this pass |

In the Place example, supplying **Tihuītz** after selecting **Iz** gives the two pieces that can be written in that order. The selected Clause order controls where they are written. | Retain in this pass |
| Branch from this / Fork | History action for an eligible whole or part | Start a separate build path from that saved state, like making a copy of a draft to try a revision. | Retain in this pass |
| Undo last build | History when a previous build on the current branch is available | Return to the preceding build on that branch. | Retain in this pass |
| Compare with another build | History disclosure | Reveal the comparison tools. | Retain in this pass |
| Find comparison builds / Build to compare | Inside the comparison disclosure. The native selector starts with **Choose another Result**. | Filter candidates and pick the second saved build. Searching keeps the current comparison selection. | Retain in this pass |

**Returning from History.** The organized **History** button opens a modal. **Close**, named **Close Your path** for assistive technology, or **Escape** dismisses it. The close handler returns focus to **History**, so a keyboard user can resume from the point where they opened the saved-build tools. An enabled **Use as Source** action also closes the modal. The renderer establishes these interactions. In isolated Chrome, opening **History** in an empty workspace showed one dialog and moved focus to **Close History**. Pressing **Escape** removed the dialog and returned focus to the **History** button. The saved-build journeys below verify History use with prepared material. **Finding prepared pieces before a session ends.** After making **Miec.** and **Cencah.** in isolated Chrome, **History** displayed both as separate builds and showed **2 exact Results; 1 branch**. It also displayed **This build history cannot be restored after reload. Continue in this tab, or apply an underlying Source to rebuild.** The writer can select the prepared quantity or adverb while both are available in the current tab. This snapshot verifies the two records, their distinct action captions, and the reload guidance. A follow-up isolated run used **Find builds** with both pieces saved and **Miec.** selected. Searching **MIEC** showed only **Miec.**. Searching **CENCAH** showed the match **Cencah.** and kept **Miec.** selected in the list. Clearing the search restored both entries. This verifies case-insensitive filtering and retention of the selected build.

**Finding a saved line by spelling.** **Find builds** and **Find comparison builds** match each search word against the displayed build label without requiring case or macrons to match. For example, a search for **tla xihuallauh** can find **Tlā xihuāllauh.** The filter keeps the selected build in the list even if it does not match. The adjacent count reports displayed entries out of all candidates, including that retained selection. Typing changes the list the writer can browse. The selected saved identity and its spelling are preserved. A focused check of the current filter confirmed macron folding, multiword matching, and selection retention. **Choosing the whole or a saved part.** **Build to work with** anchors the saved line. The **Which part to work with** buttons select a whole or a constituent beneath that anchor, and the caption shows the selected written form. In the restored address example **Tlā xihuāllauh, Tlālīxcapān!**, a writer who wants to reuse the command can choose its saved **Tlā xihuāllauh.** separately from the whole. A part without an exact saved build stays listed with its button disabled. **Use as Source** carries the chosen build forward. **Branch from this** records a new path from it while leaving the accepted sentence on display. **Branching and undo use different saved positions.** **Branch from this** uses the build selected in the History tray. It records that build as the branch anchor, and the next accepted Result starts the branch. **Undo last build** instead looks up the parent of the current build on the active branch, checks that the parent can be restored, then returns to that exact Result. For the writer looking at **Tlā xihuāllauh, Tlālīxcapān!**, selecting the saved command as a branch anchor gives the writer a place to try another continuation. Undo uses the actual parent of the current build, which can differ from the piece highlighted in the tray. The History handlers establish these two actions. The focused workspace-history fixture checks the branch anchor and exact identities recovered by undo. The command replay confirms the saved command was available.
